injuries.headline: questionable
injuries.notes: questionable

injuries.name: Samson Ebukam
injuries.headline: questionable
injuries.notes: questionable

injuries.name: Charles Snowden
injuries.headline: The Falcons signed Snowden off the Commanders' practice squad to the active roster Tuesday, Josh Kendall of The Athletic reports.
injuries.notes: Snowden has yet to appear in a regular-season game in 2026, but he'll get a fresh start in Atlanta and provide depth to the edge rusher position. He appeared in 15 regular-season games for the Raiders in 2025 and finished with 28 tackles (17 solo), including 3.0 sacks, and two pass defenses (including one interception).

injuries.name: Nick Folk
injuries.headline: Folk made his sole PAT in the Falcons' 31-23 loss to the Bears on Sunday.
injuries.notes: Folk attempted no field goals and kicked just one PAT in the loss. The kicker is still 9-for-12 on field-goal attempts and remains a perfect 13-for-13 on PATs through six regular-season contests in 2026. This was his first game all season without a field-goal attempt.

injuries.name: Zachariah Branch
injuries.headline: Branch caught both of his targets for nine yards while adding 85 yards as a kick returner during Sunday's 31-23 loss to Chicago.
injuries.notes: Branch has now caught exactly two passes in three straight games, but he has only compiled 34 total yards on those receptions. The wide receiver is merely a depth option behind the likes of Drake London, Jahan Dotson and Olamide Zaccheaus, and he's much more valuable as a return specialist for Atlanta. On the season, Branch has reeled in nine of 10 targets for 55 yards over six contests so far.

injuries.name: Michael Penix Jr.
injuries.headline: Penix completed 19 of 33 passes for 225 yards and three touchdowns with no interceptions while rushing once for one yard in the Falcons' 31-23 loss to the Bears on Sunday. He also threw two two-point conversion passes.
injuries.notes: Penix and the Falcons faced a 28-7 deficit going into the fourth quarter, but he helped bring Atlanta back with 10- and five-yard scoring tosses to Kyle Pitts and subsequent two-point conversion passes to Zachariah Branch and Drake London, respectively. Penix also connected with Jahan Dotson for a 13-yard scoring strike in the later portion of the second quarter, and Sunday's game served as Penix's first multi-TD-pass effort of the season. The third-year signal-caller also visited the medical tent in the first quarter for an undisclosed issue, but Penix appears to be healthy heading into a Week 7 home showdown against the 49ers on Sunday.

injuries.name: Tavius Robinson
injuries.headline: The Ravens placed Robinson (pectoral) on injured reserve Saturday.
injuries.notes: Robinson suffered a season-ending pectoral injury during the Ravens' Week 6 loss to the Browns. The outside linebacker will spend the rest of 2026 on IR, allowing the Ravens to carry more depth on the offensive line. The team signed offensive guard Kyle Hergel from the practice squad to the active roster in a corresponding move.

injuries.name: Tyler Huntley
injuries.headline: With Lamar Jackson (ankle) being downgraded to out, Huntley will be the Ravens' starting quarterback against the Bengals on Sunday.
injuries.notes: Jackson initially drew the questionable tag after being limited in practice all week, but he has not recovered enough from a high-ankle sprain to make his return for Sunday's AFC North showdown. Huntley will start for a third consecutive game, and the veteran quarterback will face a Bengals defense that has given up only five touchdown passes (tied for third-fewest in the league) and ranks sixth in the NFL in sacks (17).

injuries.name: Lamar Jackson
injuries.headline: Jackson (ankle) has been downgraded to out for Sunday's game against the Bengals.
injuries.notes: Jackson drew the questionable tag for Sunday's AFC North tilt after being a limited practice participant all week, but the superstar quarterback will end up missing a third consecutive game due to a high-ankle sprain. As a result, Tyler Huntley will once again start under center for the Ravens, and Jackson's next opportunity to play is Week 8 against the Bills on Sunday, Nov. 1.
injuries.vacated_opportunity_note: Takes over first-team reps under center with full pass-funnel responsibility.

injuries.name: Cam Jurgens
injuries.headline: Jurgens (concussion) does not have any injury designation ahead of Sunday's game against the Bengals.
injuries.notes: Jurgens has cleared the NFL's five-step concussion protocol and has been cleared to play in Sunday's contest. The center was acquired via a trade with the Eagles while he still had his concussion, sidelining him for his first two games with the Ravens. While Jurgens is set to suit up, starting quarterback Lamar Jackson (ankle) may need to wait until Week 8 to play with his new starting center.

injuries.name: Broderick Washington Jr.
injuries.headline: Washington (ankle) is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Bengals.
injuries.notes: Washington logged three limited sessions in Week 7 prep. The defensive lineman's practice participation looks better than in Week 6, when he missed consecutive sessions to end the week, but it remains unclear if he is set to suit up for Sunday's game. If Washington must miss consecutive weeks, Aeneas Peebles and John Jenkins will likely see more rotational defensive snaps in Sunday's contest.

injuries.name: Jaylinn Hawkins
injuries.headline: Hawkins (knee) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Bengals, Cordell Woodland of 105.7 The Fan Baltimore reports.
injuries.notes: Hawkins popped up on Wednesday's practice report as a limited participant due to a knee injury, which prevented him from practicing each of the next two days. He won't play Sunday, and head coach Jesse Minter suggested Friday that Hawkins could be sidelined beyond Week 7. In Hawkins' absence, K'Von Wallace and Keondre Jackson figure to be the top candidates to start alongside Malaki Starks at safety.

injuries.name: Andrew Vorhees
injuries.headline: Vorhees (foot) was a full participant at the Ravens' practice Thursday.
injuries.notes: Vorhees was able to be upgraded to a full participant after opening the week with a limited practice Wednesday. The offensive lineman has missed the last two games while recovering from a foot injury, but he appears to be on track to play Sunday versus the Bengals.

injuries.name: Matt Hibner
injuries.headline: Hibner (hand) was a full participant at practice Thursday.
injuries.notes: Hibner managed a full practice Thursday for the first time since he hurt his hand back in Week 5 at Atlanta, suggesting he'll more than likely be available in Week 7 versus the Bengals. Before getting hurt, he was operating as Baltimore's secondary tight end, filling a complementary role relative to veteran starter Mark Andrews.

injuries.name: Rashod Bateman
injuries.headline: Bateman (shoulder) was a full participant in Thursday's practice.
injuries.notes: A limited practice participant to begin the week after he exited this past Sunday's loss to the Browns due to the shoulder issue, Bateman cleared up any concern about his health by taking every rep during Thursday's session. While he'll be ready to play Sunday versus the Bengals, Bateman's standing as the No. 2 wideout on the depth chart behind Zay Flowers could be threatened after rookie Ja'Kobi Lane produced well in his return from injured reserve last week, logging four catches for 40 yards on five targets.

injuries.name: T.J. Tampa
injuries.headline: The Ravens designated Tampa (toe/ankle) to return from injured reserve Wednesday.
injuries.notes: Tampa was placed on IR in mid-September due to what was diagnosed at the time as a knee injury, but Wednesday's practice report listed ankle and toe injuries for the third-year defensive back. He was a limited participant in his return, and he'll need to be activated from IR in order to be available for Sunday's AFC North tilt against the Bengals. Tampa's return would give the Ravens extra depth in the secondary and another contributor on special teams.

injuries.name: Kyle Hamilton
injuries.headline: Hamilton finished Sunday's 13-10 loss to the Browns with seven tackles (six solo).
injuries.notes: Hamilton played every single defensive snap for the third time in six games. Three of his seven tackles resulted in a loss, and he finished third on the team in combined stops behind Trenton Simpson and Jaylinn Hawkins (eight each). Hamilton has recorded at least seven combined tackles in four of his last five games and is up to 46 tackles (32 solo), four pass defenses (one interception) and one forced fumble.

injuries.name: Roquan Smith
injuries.headline: Smith logged five tackles (three solo), including 1.0 sacks, during Sunday's 13-10 loss to the Browns.
injuries.notes: Smith was credited with his second sack of the season when he took down Deshaun Watson late in the first quarter, which led to the Browns punting the ball away two plays later. Smith's sack total is already his most in a season since the 2022 campaign (4.5 across 17 regular-season games), when he suited up for both the Bears and Ravens. His 47 combined tackles leads the Ravens and is tied with Dane Belton and Jihaad Campbell for 17th-most in the NFL.

injuries.name: Justice Hill
injuries.headline: Hill caught all three of his targets for nine yards during the Ravens' 13-10 loss to the Browns on Sunday.
injuries.notes: Hill was on the field for 24 of the Ravens' 57 offensive snaps (42.1 percent), which wasn't far behind lead back Derrick Henry (33). That was more due to game script, as the Ravens' offense struggled to move the ball down the field against a tough Browns defense. The offensive outlook for Hill and the rest of Baltimore's skill position players would improve dramatically if Lamar Jackson (ankle) is cleared to play in Week 7 against the Bengals on Oct. 25.

injuries.name: Tyler Loop
injuries.headline: Loop converted one his two field-goal attempts and his lone extra-point try during Baltimore's loss to Cleveland on Sunday.
injuries.notes: Loop missed a 49-yard field goal in the fourth quarter, which ended up being the difference in the three-point loss. This was his first missed kick of the season, and he will look to bounce back next week versus the Bengals.

injuries.name: Mark Andrews
injuries.headline: Andrews caught one of three targets for four yards during the Ravens' 13-10 loss to the Browns on Sunday.
injuries.notes: Andrews saw only three pass attempts from Tyler Huntley on Sunday, and it was the first time that the veteran tight end saw less than five targets in a game this season. Andrews' 41 offensive snaps were most among Ravens tight ends, but his receiving line was below rookie fifth-rounder Josh Cuevas (4-44-1 on five targets). Baltimore will head back home for Week 7 against the Bengals on Oct. 25, and Andrews' scoring floor will be boosted if Lamar Jackson (ankle) is cleared to return from a two-game absence.

injuries.name: Ja'Kobi Lane
injuries.headline: Lane brought in four of five targets for 40 yards in the Ravens' 13-10 loss to the Browns on Sunday.
injuries.notes: Lane was making his return from a four-game stint on IR due to a wrist injury, and he set new career highs across the board after having gotten hurt in Week 1. He tied for second in receptions and targets while slotting in third in receiving yards on the afternoon for the Ravens. Lane's chemistry with Tyler Huntley was encouraging, but the rookie wideout's fantasy upside could truly be unlocked once he has a stretch of games to work with Lamar Jackson (ankle).

injuries.name: Zay Flowers
injuries.headline: Flowers brought in six of 11 targets for 66 yards and rushed once for one yard in the Ravens' 13-10 loss to the Browns on Sunday.
injuries.notes: Flowers set the pace for the Ravens in receptions, receiving yards and targets on the afternoon, displaying solid chemistry with Tyler Huntley once again. The speedy wideout has no fewer than five catches and 53 receiving yards in any game this season, and he's recorded a 14-118-0 line over the last two games alone with Huntley under center. Flowers will remain a must-play wideout regardless of who's helming the Ravens offense in a Week 7 home matchup against the division-rival Bengals next Sunday.

injuries.name: Derrick Henry
injuries.headline: Henry rushed 17 times for 58 yards and brought in his only target for two yards in the Ravens' 13-10 loss to the Browns on Sunday. He also lost a fumble.
injuries.notes: Henry looked like he was on his way to one of his signature performances when he rattled off 11- and 17-yard gains on Baltimore's opening possession, but the veteran back found running room at a premium for most of the rest of the contest. Henry finished without a touchdown for the second straight game and tallied his lowest rushing yardage total of the campaign, while his early fourth-quarter fumble led to a Browns game-tying touchdown. Henry will aim to bounce back in a Week 7 home divisional matchup against the Bengals next Sunday.

injuries.name: Josh Cuevas
injuries.headline: Cuevas caught four of five targets for 44 yards and a touchdown during Sunday's 13-10 loss to Cleveland.
injuries.notes: Cuevas got the scoring started Sunday, reeling in a two-yard score from quarterback Tyler Huntley in the first quarter. The touchdown was the first of his career, and he finished tied for second on the team in both targets and catches in Week 6. Cuevas has now reeled in multiple passes in consecutive games, but he will continue to be hard to count on from a fantasy perspective as long as starting tight end Mark Andrews is available.

injuries.name: C.J. Gardner-Johnson
injuries.headline: reserve-sus
injuries.notes: reserve-sus

injuries.name: Sam Franklin Jr.
injuries.headline: The NFL reduced Franklin's discipline from a one-game suspension to a fine of $14,926, Adam Schefter of ESPN reports.
injuries.notes: Franklin was disciplined by the league for allegedly spitting at an opponent late in the fourth quarter of the Bills' Week 6 win over the Raiders. The decision has been altered to a fine, and with the Bills on a bye, the Temple product will be available for Week 8 against the Ravens on Sunday, Nov. 1.

injuries.name: Dorian Williams
injuries.headline: Williams logged five tackles (three solo) and one pass defensed for an interception in the Bills' 33-30 win over the Raiders on Sunday.
injuries.notes: Despite a relatively poor showing from a struggling Bills defense, Williams picked off Raiders quarterback Kirk Cousins in the third quarter of Sunday's contest. The linebacker's stolen possession, the first interception of his NFL career, led to the Bills extending the lead from 16-13 to 23-13 with 6:22 remaining in the third quarter.

injuries.name: Davison Igbinosun
injuries.headline: Defensive coordinator Jim Leonhard praised Igbinosun's play earlier this week and plans to keep giving the rookie a good amount of playing time, Alec White of the Bills' official site reports. Said Leonard, "I think what he's done the last couple weeks, he's definitely earned a high majority of the snaps at the corner position. I know what I'm getting, play in and play out."
injuries.notes: Igbinosun, a second-round rookie out of Ohio State, has seen 64 or more percent of the defensive snaps in each of the past three games as he continues to make his mark at the NFL level. That's more than teammate Maxwell Hairston in each of the past two, so IGB may be working his way into a starter's role opposite star corner Christian Benford. Igbinosun had seven total tackles in Week 6, and he had three passes defensed in the Week 7 win over the Raiders.

injuries.name: Dawson Knox
injuries.headline: Knox caught his only target for no gain during Sunday's 33-30 win at Las Vegas.
injuries.notes: He again played about as many snaps at tight end Sunday (47) as did starter Dalton Kincaid (49), but Knox continued to function mostly as a blocker. He has yet to draw more than three targets in a game this season, and he'll probably remain on the periphery of the passing offense as long as Kincaid is still available.

injuries.name: DJ Moore
injuries.headline: questionable
injuries.notes: questionable
injuries.vacated_opportunity_note: Expands to high-volume target progression and 2-WR/3-WR set route participation.

injuries.name: Ed Oliver
injuries.headline: questionable
injuries.notes: questionable

injuries.name: Tyler Bass
injuries.headline: Bass converted all four of his field-goal attempts and all three of his extra-point tries during Buffalo's win over the Raiders on Sunday.
injuries.notes: Bass was dominant during the victory, as he was perfect on all of his kicks. The 29-year-old continues to have a strong season, as he has missed just two kicks (both PATs) across his first six appearances.

injuries.name: Ty Johnson
injuries.headline: Johnson logged a three-yard carry and caught both of his targets for 24 yards during the Bills' 33-30 win over the Raiders on Sunday.
injuries.notes: Johnson and Ray Davis each saw only one carry during Sunday's win, with lead back James Cook turning 22 carries into 95 yards and a touchdown. Johnson was still involved somewhat in the passing game, and through four games he has 12 catches on as many targets for 155 yards. The veteran running back will continue to operate in a rotational role on offense, but his workload would expand significantly if Cook ever misses time. The Bills are on a bye for Week 7, and their next game will take place in Week 8 against the Ravens on Sunday, Nov. 1.

injuries.name: Joshua Palmer
injuries.headline: Palmer caught one of two targets for 37 yards during Buffalo's 33-30 win over Las Vegas on Sunday.
injuries.notes: Palmer was cleared to return from a one-game absence due to a shoulder injury, and his 17 offensive snaps were last among the Bills' active wide receivers with DJ Moore (shoulder) sidelined. Palmer connected with Josh Allen on a 37-yard pass late in the first quarter to move the Bills into opposing territory, leading to a 28-yard field goal by Tyler Bass nine plays later. Three of Palmer's four catches this season have gone for 30-plus yards, but he isn't a featured part of the Bills'offense and will see his role decrease once Moore is cleared to return. Buffalo is on a bye for Week 7 and will return to action for Week 8 against Baltimore on Sunday, Nov. 1.

injuries.name: Ray Davis
injuries.headline: Davis logged a four-yard carry and a five-yard catch on his lone target while returning three kickoffs for 85 yards during the Bills' 33-30 win over the Raiders on Sunday.
injuries.notes: Davis made his impact felt early with a 40-yard return on the game's opening kickoff, which set the Bills offense up at midfield and led to a 44-yard field goal by Tyler Bass nine plays later. Both of Davis' touches on offense came on back-to-back plays in the second quarter, and his nine offensive snaps were behind both Ty Johnson (12) and James Cook (45). Davis isn't much of a factor offensively, but he would be in line for a larger role if one or both of Cook and Johnson miss time. The Bills will enjoy their bye week before hosting the Ravens in Week 8 on Sunday, Nov. 1.

injuries.name: Dalton Kincaid
injuries.headline: Kincaid (ribs) returned to Sunday's 33-30 win at Las Vegas and finished with seven catches (on eight targets) for 38 yards.
injuries.notes: Kincaid missed some time from late in the third quarter and into the fourth to be evaluated in the sideline tent, but he got back on the field with 8:01 remaining and added one more reception to his final line. Overall, he paced the Bills in catches and targets, but he ended Week 6 with his lowest YPC (5.4) of the campaign. The Bills have a Week 7 bye, so he'll have plenty of time to heal up for Buffalo's next game Sunday, Nov. 1 against the Ravens.

injuries.name: Keon Coleman
injuries.headline: Coleman brought in four of six targets for 59 yards and a touchdown in the Bills' 33-30 win over the Raiders on Sunday.
injuries.notes: Coleman led the Bills in receiving yards on the afternoon with the help of a 21-yard grab and a 12-yard touchdown reception with just over six minutes remaining in the third quarter. The score was Coleman's third of the season, with the previous two having come in each of the prior pair of contests against the Patriots and Rams. The oft-maligned 2024 second-round pick appears to be picking up some momentum in his third season, as Coleman already has a 19-283-3 line on 24 targets while helping make up for the multiple absences of DJ Moore (shoulder).

injuries.name: Khalil Shakir
injuries.headline: Shakir brought in four of six targets for 34 yards and a touchdown in the Bills' 33-30 win over the Raiders on Sunday.
injuries.notes: Shakir posted his second-lowest yardage figure of the season, but the talented veteran recorded his first touchdown of the campaign on a nine-yard grab just past the midway point of the second quarter. His target total also tied for his second highest of the campaign, a figure he'd reached on two other occasions. The fifth-year pro should continue to garner his fair share of Josh Allen's attention moving forward, although Shakir's targets could take a slight hit if DJ Moore (shoulder) returns for a Week 8 home matchup against the Ravens on Sunday, Nov. 1, following a Week 7 bye.

injuries.name: Josh Allen
injuries.headline: Allen completed 23 of 33 passes for 255 yards with two touchdowns and no interceptions and rushed five times for one yard in the Bills' 33-30 win over the Raiders on Sunday.
injuries.notes: Allen once again operated without DJ Moore (shoulder), although he did have another deep threat in Joshua Palmer back from his own shoulder issue. The one-time MVP signal-caller spread the ball around to eight different targets, and Allen ultimately played without Dalton Kincaid (rib) for a spell in the second half as well. Allen's passing numbers haven't been particularly impressive since a 334-yard showing against the Texans back in Week 1 as first-year head coach Joe Brady looks to run a balanced attack. However, the prolific quarterback still has 1,504 passing yards with a 9:4 TD:INT and another 240 rushing yards and eight additional scores going into a Week 8 home showdown with the Ravens on Sunday, Nov. 1, following a Week 7 bye.

injuries.name: James Cook III
injuries.headline: Cook rushed 22 times for 95 yards and a touchdown and brought in all three targets for 58 yards in the Bills' 33-30 win over the Raiders on Sunday.
injuries.notes: Cook put together productive runs throughout the afternoon, and he added a 26-yard reception as part of an impressive day as a pass catcher. The standout running back extended his streak of games with at least one rushing touchdown to five as well, crossing the goal line from three yards out with 4:43 remaining in the contest. Cook has put up between 75 and 154 rushing yards in the last five games after opening the season with a modest 57-yard showing on the ground against the Texans, and he's already amassed 716 yards from scrimmage over six games going into a Week 8 home showdown on Sunday, Nov. 1, against the Ravens following a Week 7 bye.

injuries.name: Bradley Chubb
injuries.headline: Chubb (ribs) has returned to Sunday's game against the Raiders, Jay Skurski of The Buffalo News reports.
injuries.notes: Chubb exited the second quarter of the game with a rib injury but was expected to return to the game. The outside linebacker is back in action after a short absence and is playing through the minor injury.

injuries.name: Dee Alford
injuries.headline: Alford (ankle) is active for Sunday's game against the Raiders.
injuries.notes: Alford was limited throughout Week 6 prep after missing the Bills' Monday night win over the Rams with an ankle injury. The slot cornerback is back in action and ready to cover Brock Bowers in the slot during Sunday's game against the Raiders.

injuries.name: Landon Jackson
injuries.headline: Jackson (knee) was a full participant in Wednesday's walkthrough practice.
injuries.notes: Jackson missed the Bills' Week 5 overtime win against the Rams due to a knee injury. The defensive end appears to have recovered from the injury after sitting out Week 5 and should be set to suit up for Sunday's game against the Raiders if he can continue to practice in full.

injuries.name: Christian Benford
injuries.headline: Benford (toe) does not carry an injury designation into Monday night's game against the Rams, Joe Buscaglia of The Athletic reports.
injuries.notes: Benford has been given the green light to return from a one-game absence due to a toe injury that he sustained during the Bills' Week 3 win over the Chargers. He'll resume his starting spot at outside cornerback, and while rookie first-rounder Maxwell Hairston will start opposite Benford, rookie second-rounder Davison Igbinosun will also be involved in the Bills' secondary, per Nick Suss of ESPN.com.

injuries.name: Thomas Incoom
injuries.headline: Incoom (calf) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Buccaneers.
injuries.notes: Incoom was unable to practice all week due to a calf injury that he picked up against the Eagles in Week 6, and his next chance to play is Thursday against the Packers. The Panthers will have less edge depth Sunday because of the absences of both Incoom and Jaelan Phillips (hamstring).

injuries.name: Jaelan Phillips
injuries.headline: Phillips (hamstring) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Buccaneers.
injuries.notes: Phillips aggravated a hamstring injury during the Panthers' Week 6 win over the Eagles. The injury prevented him from practicing during Week 7 prep, and his absence means Princely Umanmielen will likely start opposite Patrick Jones at the edge rusher position. Phillips' next chance to play is Thursday against the Packers at Lambeau Field.

injuries.name: Monroe Freeling
injuries.headline: questionable
injuries.notes: questionable

injuries.name: Devin Lloyd
injuries.headline: Lloyd recorded four tackles (three solo), including 1.0 sacks, during the Panthers' 25-14 win over the Eagles in Week 6.
injuries.notes: Lloyd was responsible for one of the Panthers' three sacks in Week 6, with the fifth-year linebacker taking down Tanner McKee in the third quarter for a six-yard loss. Lloyd is up to 2.0 sacks through four games, which matches his career high that he set in 2024 with the Jaguars across 16 regular-season games.

injuries.name: Bobby Okereke
injuries.headline: Okereke recorded eight tackles (seven solo), including 1.0 sacks, and two pass defenses during the Panthers' 25-14 win over the Eagles in Week 6.
injuries.notes: Okereke led the Panthers in both combined and solo tackles in Week 6, and he set the tone early for the defense by sacking Tanner McKee on the Eagles' first offensive play of the game. It was Okereke's first sack of the season and matches his total across 17 regular-season games with the Giants in 2025. The veteran linebacker is up to 34 tackles (21 solo), four pass defenses (including one interception) and one forced fumble through five regular-season games.

injuries.name: AJ Dillon
injuries.headline: Dillon (ankle) was estimated as a full participant on the Panthers' official injury report Wednesday, Darin Gantt of the team's official site reports.
injuries.notes: Dillon sat out Sunday's game at Philadelphia because of an ankle injury, but it looks like he's on pace to return to action in Week 7. He figures to continue to play a change-of-pace role in Carolina's backfield behind bell cow Chuba Hubbard.

injuries.name: Anthony Tyus III
injuries.headline: The Panthers signed Tyus off their practice squad to the active roster Tuesday, Joe Person of The Athletic reports.
injuries.notes: It's the second time this season that Tyus has been signed to the Panthers' 53-man roster. The second-year pro was elevated from the practice squad for each of the team's last two games to contribute on special teams while providing depth in the backfield, because of the absences of AJ Dillon (ankle) and Jonathon Brooks (abdomen, IR).

injuries.name: Ryan Fitzgerald
injuries.headline: Fitzgerald made both of his field-goal attempts but missed one of two PATs in the Panthers' 25-14 win over the Eagles on Sunday.
injuries.notes: Fitzgerald converted field-goal attempts from 47 and 52 yards but continues to struggle with PATs. The kicker missed two extra-point attempts in Week 4 against the Lions as well. Fitzgerald remains a perfect 11-for-11 on field-goal attempts while dropping to 11-for-15 on extra points through five contests in the 2026 regular season.

injuries.name: Jalen Coker
injuries.headline: Coker brought in six of 13 targets for 97 yards in the Panthers' 25-14 win over the Eagles on Sunday. He also committed a fumble recovered by Carolina.
injuries.notes: Making his return from a one-game absence due to a quadriceps injury, Coker picked up right where he left off while tying for the team lead in receptions and setting the pace in both receiving yards and targets. He also had a game-long 32-yard catch, and he now has at least six grabs in three of his first four games. With a 24-319-2 line through four contests, the speedy third-year wideout is well on his way to setting new career bests as he heads into a Week 7 home matchup against the Buccaneers on Sunday.

injuries.name: Bryce Young
injuries.headline: Young completed 20 of 39 passes for 281 yards with two touchdowns and no interceptions and added three rushes for six yards in the Panthers' 25-14 win over the Eagles on Sunday.
injuries.notes: Young's pair of scoring tosses went to Tommy Tremble from 12 and 19 yards out in the second and fourth quarters, respectively. The 2023 first overall pick's multi-touchdown effort was his fourth of the season, and Young hasn't thrown for fewer than Sunday's total in any of his five games while also generating a stellar 11:2 TD:INT. Young and the Panthers next take aim at the Buccaneers defense when Tampa Bay pays a visit for a Week 7 divisional showdown on Sunday.

injuries.name: Tetairoa McMillan
injuries.headline: McMillan secured six of nine targets for 86 yards in the Panthers' 25-14 win over the Eagles on Sunday.
injuries.notes: McMillan tied for the team lead in receptions with Jalen Coker while finishing second to his talented position mate in receiving yards and targets. The 2025 first-round pick was coming off a career-best 14-catch, 192-yard performance that also included two touchdowns against the Lions back in Week 4, and he's gone for at least 75 receiving yards in four of his first five games of the campaign as a Week 7 home divisional showdown against the Buccaneers approaches.

injuries.name: Chuba Hubbard
injuries.headline: Hubbard rushed 28 times for 120 yards and a touchdown and brought in one of two targets for one yard in the Panthers' 25-14 win over the Eagles on Sunday.
injuries.notes: Hubbard thoroughly dominated the Panthers' ground attack with AJ Dillon (ankle) sidelined and finished with his highest rushing workload of the campaign. Hubbard also hit the 120-yard mark on the ground for the second straight contest, and he added his fourth rush TD on a one-yard run early in the fourth quarter. After combining for 102 rushing yards in his first two games of the season, Hubbard has run for 324 yards at 4.8 yards per carry and added a 6-36-0 receiving line over the subsequent trio of contests heading into a Week 7 home divisional clash with the Buccaneers on Sunday.

injuries.name: Darren Waller
injuries.headline: Waller failed to catch either of his two targets in Sunday's 25-14 win over the Eagles.
injuries.notes: Waller dealt with a toe injury during the practice week and ended up playing behind both Tommy Tremble and Mitchell Evans in this one, as Tremble was the big producer in the box score, catching a pair of red-zone touchdowns. Waller is one of the many touchdown-or-bust fantasy options at the tight end position.

injuries.name: Tommy Tremble
injuries.headline: Tremble caught all four targets for 46 yards and two touchdowns in Sunday's 25-14 win over the Eagles.
injuries.notes: Tremble played 54 snaps to Mitchell Evans' 43 and Darren Waller's 36, and Tremble ran the most routes of the trio. His touchdowns were both of the red-zone variety, as he scored from 12 and 19 yards out. The tight end entered Sunday with 11 catches for 82 yards on 15 targets, so he's not worth chasing in fantasy ahead of next Sunday's date with the Bucs.

injuries.name: Damien Lewis
injuries.headline: Lewis (elbow) is active for Sunday's game against the Eagles, Darin Gantt of the Panthers' official site reports.
injuries.notes: Lewis was diagnosed with a UCL tear in his elbow following the Panthers' Week 3 loss to the Browns. He was sidelined for Week 4 against the Lions, but with extra rest thanks to the Week 5 bye, Lewis has been cleared to return for Sunday's game. He'll reclaim his starting role at left guard from Corey Bullock.

injuries.name: Taylor Moton
injuries.headline: Moton (illness) is active for Sunday's game against the Eagles, Darin Gantt of the Panthers' official site reports.
injuries.notes: Moton was activated from the reserve/non-football illness list Saturday, and he's been cleared to make his 2026 debut Sunday after fully recovering from blood clots in his lungs. He figures to start at right tackle Sunday, especially with Monroe Freeling (knee) inactive.

injuries.name: Tershawn Wharton
injuries.headline: Wharton (neck) is active for Sunday's game against the Eagles, Darin Gantt of the Panthers' official site reports.
injuries.notes: Wharton opened the regular season on the reserve/PUP list while recovering from neck surgery that he underwent in May. He was activated from the PUP list Saturday, and the seventh-year pro has been cleared to make his 2026 debut Sunday.

injuries.name: Trevor Etienne
injuries.headline: Etienne (ankle) is active for Sunday's game against the Eagles, Darin Gantt of the Panthers' official site reports.
injuries.notes: Etienne was activated from injured reserve Saturday, and the second-year running back has been cleared to make his 2026 debut Sunday after missing the first four games of the regular season due to an ankle injury. He could operate as the Panthers' RB2 behind Chuba Hubbard, given the absences of both AJ Dillon (ankle) and Jonathon Brooks (abdomen, IR).

injuries.name: Jonathon Brooks
injuries.headline: Brooks (core) was seen jogging at practice Thursday, Sheena Quick of Fox Sports Radio 1340 reports.
injuries.notes: Brooks appears to be making incremental progress in his recovery from core muscle surgery, though he wasn't in uniform Thursday and has yet to be cleared for participation in practice drills while he remains on injured reserve. The 2024 second-round pick has suited up for just five of a possible 38 regular-season games in his career and will miss a minimum of two additional games before he's eligible to return, though his absence could linger beyond then. Chuba Hubbard has worked as the clear lead back for the Panthers, with AJ Dillon (ankle) siphoning off less work than Brooks had been prior to getting hurt.

injuries.name: Cam Jackson
injuries.headline: The Panthers placed Jackson (shoulder) on injured reserve Tuesday, Darin Gantt of the team's official site reports.
injuries.notes: Jackson will miss the remainder of the campaign after undergoing shoulder surgery. He was also nursing a knee injury and will now shift his focus to getting healthy for the 2027 campaign.

injuries.name: Anthony Johnson Jr.
injuries.headline: out
injuries.notes: out

injuries.name: Sam Roush
injuries.headline: Roush is expected to get more work on offense after Cole Kmet (knee) landed on injured reserve Friday.
injuries.notes: Roush didn't catch a pass against New England on Thursday, marking his third straight game without a reception. However, he's currently the only healthy tight end on the Bears' roster aside from starter Colston Loveland, so Roush figures to be in line for an expanded role moving forward. With that said, Loveland has logged 57 or more receiving yards and six or more catches three of the past four weeks and is clearly the Bears' go-to tight end in the passing game, so Roush's anticipated increase of offensive snaps doesn't necessarily make him a viable option in fantasy.

injuries.name: Kalif Raymond
injuries.headline: Raymond did not catch either of his two targets and returned one punt for seven yards Thursday in a 30-24 win over New England.
injuries.notes: Raymond started at WR for Chicago and got plenty of playing time, logging 48 of 69 snaps on offense. However, he was unable to make an impact, finishing without a catch for the first time this season. Top wideouts Luther Burden and Rome Odunze combined for eight catches, 199 yards and a touchdown Thursday, and Raymond figures to compete for scraps whenever that pair is healthy.

injuries.name: Roschon Johnson
injuries.headline: Johnson rushed twice for 13 yards in the Bears' 30-24 victory over the Patriots on Thursday.
injuries.notes: Johnson played just 10 offensive snaps to D'Andre Swift's 54 in the contest. The running back did not see much action as he filled in for the injured Kyle Monangai (toe) as a rotational option for the Bears' offense. Johnson also saw one snap with the special teams unit.

injuries.name: Montez Sweat
injuries.headline: The NFL reinstated Sweat on Friday after he served a two-game suspension for violating the league's performance-enhancing substances policy.
injuries.notes: The defensive end is set to return to practice in Week 8 and should play in the team's Monday Night Football showdown against the Seahawks. Sweat has logged seven tackles (two solo), including 2.0 sacks, over his five regular-season appearances so far in 2026.

injuries.name: Cole Kmet
injuries.headline: The Bears placed Kmet (knee) on injured reserve Friday.
injuries.notes: Kmet suffered a season-ending right knee injury during the fourth quarter of the Bears' 30-24 win over the Patriots on Thursday. Even with the emergence of Colston Loveland, Kmet was still a key piece in Chicago's offense as a run blocker, and he'll end his 2026 regular season with a 10-87-1 receiving line (on 14 targets) across seven games. Rookie third-rounder Sam Roush is the only other healthy tight end on the 53-man roster other than Loveland, so the Bears could look to bolster the position group by trade or free agency.
injuries.vacated_opportunity_note: Assumes inline snaps and high-leverage red-zone target share.

injuries.name: Rome Odunze
injuries.headline: Odunze brought in four of five targets for 69 yards in the Bears' 30-24 win over the Patriots on Thursday.
injuries.notes: Odunze was encouragingly efficient in the high-scoring win, but he once again saw fellow wideout Luther Burden be more productive. Burden's 130 receiving yards led the Bears on the night, and Odunze appears to have fallen into more of a de facto No. 2 role at this point in the season. Odunze still carries solid fantasy value, however, and he'll carry a 24-381-0 line on 38 targets into a Week 8 road showdown against the Seahawks on Monday night, Nov. 2.

injuries.name: Colston Loveland
injuries.headline: Loveland secured seven of 12 targets for 69 yards and a touchdown during the Bears' 30-24 win over the Patriots on Thursday.
injuries.notes: The second-year tight end continued to shake out of his early-season slump, putting together his second fantasy-friendly performance in a five-day span. Loveland led the Bears in receptions and targets on the night with figures that also qualified as season highs, and he added his second touchdown in five days on a 12-yard grab early in the third quarter. He has a 13-134-2 line in the last two games alone and should continue playing a key role in a Week 8 road showdown against the Seahawks on Monday night, Nov. 2, and he could be in line for even heavier involvement if Cole Kmet (knee) is unable to suit up.

injuries.name: Cairo Santos
injuries.headline: Santos went 3-for-4 on field-goal tries and made all three of his extra-point attempts in Thursday's 30-24 win over New England.
injuries.notes: Santos put the first points on the board with a 43-yard field goal in the first quarter and added a 31-yarder in the second. He had a chance to give Chicago a two-score lead midway through the fourth quarter but clanged a 53-yard attempt off the right upright. However, Santos atoned for that miss in dramatic fashion, knocking in a 58-yard field goal -- the longest make of his career -- with less than two minutes remaining to essentially seal the win for the Bears. He's now 11-for-15 on field-goal tries this season, including 3-for-5 from 50-plus yards.

injuries.name: D'Andre Swift
injuries.headline: Swift rushed 22 times for 78 yards and a touchdown and brought in all four targets for 12 yards in the Bears' 30-24 win over the Patriots on Thursday.
injuries.notes: With Kyle Monangai (toe/thumb) out for a third straight game, Swift once again handled a workhorse role and parlayed it into some solid production. Swift's rushing yardage total was his third highest of the season, and the veteran back got into the end zone for the third straight game on a four-yard run late in the first quarter. He's up to seven rushing touchdowns on the season, but his touches will take a hit if Monangai is able to get healthy enough over the extended time between Thursday's game and a Week 8 road matchup against the Seahawks on Monday night, Nov. 2 to suit up for that contest.

injuries.name: Luther Burden III
injuries.headline: Burden brought in all four targets for 130 yards and a touchdown and rushed once for seven yards in the Bears' 30-24 win over the Patriots on Thursday.
injuries.notes: Burden comfortably led the Bears in receiving yards with the second-highest total of his career, and he added his second touchdown catch of the season on a 24-yard grab just before halftime. He also had a game-long 58-yard catch late in the first quarter to set up a D'Andre Swift four-yard touchdown one play later, and the fleet-footed receiver has accumulated 225 of his 491 receiving yards on the season in the last two games alone. Burden has arguably overtaken Rome Odunze as Chicago's most explosive pass-catching weapon, and he should play a critical role again in a Week 8 road showdown against the Seahawks on Monday night, Nov. 2.

injuries.name: Caleb Williams
injuries.headline: Williams completed 22 of 33 passes for 308 yards with two touchdowns and no interceptions while rushing five times for 18 yards in the Bears' 30-24 win over the Patriots on Thursday.
injuries.notes: Williams spearheaded another prolific performance for the Bears offense, leading his squad to another 30-point tally while eclipsing the 300-yard mark for the second time in five days. He tied his season high with 9.3 yards per attempt, and he accomplished his stellar numbers while focusing on a tight pool of five targets. The 2024 first overall pick's two touchdown passes went to Luther Burden (24 yards) and Colston Loveland (12 yards), marking Williams' first multi-TD tally since Week 1. Williams appears to be clicking on all cylinders in his second season in head coach Ben Johnson's aggressive offense, now having completed 71.0 percent of his passes for 1,020 yards through four games heading into a Week 8 road showdown with the defending champion Seahawks on Monday night, Nov. 2.

injuries.name: Malik Muhammad II
injuries.headline: Muhammad (toe) is doubtful to return to Thursday night's contest against the Patriots.
injuries.notes: Muhammad is dealing with a toe injury, and he will now likely be forced to watch the remainder of the game from the Bears' sideline. In Muhammad's absence, Josh Blackwell and Clark Phillips are both candidates to see an increase in workload at cornerback.

injuries.name: Tyrique Stevenson Sr.
injuries.headline: Stevenson (hip) is active for Thursday night's contest against New England.
injuries.notes: Stevenson will make his return to action after missing the team's Week 6 win over Atlanta while nursing a hip injury that he suffered a week prior versus Green Bay. The 26-year-old will be back in his starting role at cornerback, and his primary task Thursday night may be slowing down A.J. Brown.

injuries.name: T.J. Edwards
injuries.headline: Edwards (hamstring) is inactive for Thursday night's matchup against New England.
injuries.notes: Edwards is still working his way back from a hamstring injury that he suffered in Week 5 against the Packers, and he will now be forced to miss a second straight contest. In his absence, Noah Sewell will stand to draw the start at middle linebacker versus the Patriots.

injuries.name: Case Keenum
injuries.headline: Keenum (coach's decision) is inactive but will operate as the Bears' emergency third quarterback for Thursday night's matchup against the Patriots.
injuries.notes: Keenum will serve as the No. 3 QB for the second straight week while Tyson Bagent slots in as the primary backup behind starter Caleb Williams. Keenum will only be eligible to enter the contest if both Williams and Bagent are forced out of the game.

injuries.name: Jayden Loving
injuries.headline: inactive
injuries.notes: inactive

injuries.name: Nick McCloud
injuries.headline: inactive
injuries.notes: inactive

injuries.name: Jordan McFadden
injuries.headline: inactive
injuries.notes: inactive

injuries.name: Kyle Monangai
injuries.headline: inactive
injuries.notes: inactive
injuries.vacated_opportunity_note: Primary beneficiary of vacated early-down carries & red-zone volume if starter is sidelined.

injuries.name: Jonah Jackson
injuries.headline: Jackson (hip/quadricep) does not have any injury designation ahead of Thursday night's game against the Patriots.
injuries.notes: Jackson picked up multiple injuries in the Bears' Week 6 win over the Falcons. The offensive guard was able to upgrade his practice participation in every session during the team's short turnaround ahead of Thursday Night Football and is all set to suit up for the contest against the Patriots.

injuries.name: Jack Sanborn
injuries.headline: Sanborn (concussion) is officially listed as out for Thursday's game versus the Patriots.
injuries.notes: The Bears held only walkthrough practices ahead of Thursday's contest, but Sanborn was estimated as a nonparticipant Monday, Tuesday and Wednesday, and he'll now miss his first game of the season in Week 7. Most of his snaps so far in 2026 have come on special teams, so Chicago will have to find a way to try to replace his production in that phase.

injuries.name: Keyshaun Elliott
injuries.headline: Elliott (quadriceps) was estimated as a full participant on the Bears' official injury report Monday.
injuries.notes: Elliott has sat out Chicago's last two games due to a quad injury, but it looks like he's on track to return to the field in Week 7 versus the Patriots. All 56 of the rookie's snaps so far this season have come on special teams.

injuries.name: Kyler Gordon
injuries.headline: Gordon posted four solo tackles, including 3.0 sacks, and two forced fumbles during the Bears' 31-23 win over the Falcons on Sunday.
injuries.notes: Gordon was cleared to make his 2026 debut Sunday after fully recovering from a calf injury stemming from the offseason. He played only 17 of 46 defensive snaps (41.5 percent), but he was the most impactful Bears defender. Two of his three sacks on Michael Penix resulted in fumbles, the second of which was recovered by Chicago late in the fourth quarter to seal the win. The Bears will operate on short rest in their Week 7 tilt against the Patriots on Thursday, so it wouldn't be surprising if Gordon operates under a snap count for at least one more game.

injuries.name: Jahdae Walker
injuries.headline: Walker went without a target while playing 10 of the Bears' 77 snaps on offense in Sunday's 31-23 win over the Falcons.
injuries.notes: Walker's afternoon came to an end just after the start of the fourth quarter, when he was ejected for headbutting a Falcons player at the end of a kickoff return. He was assessed his second 15-yard penalty of the day as a result, with his first coming on a roughing-the-kicker charge back in the third quarter. Walker will remain a key part of the Bears' special-teams units heading into a Week 7 matchup with the Patriots, but he's buried on the depth chart at receiver and isn't likely to see extended playing time on offense anytime soon.

injuries.name: Kyle Dugger
injuries.headline: Dugger (quadriceps) doesn't have an injury designation against the Ravens on Sunday, Mike Garafolo of NFL Network reports.
injuries.notes: Dugger has been cleared to return from a two-game absence due to a quadriceps injury. He figures to see most of his playing time on special teams while operating in a depth role in the secondary behind starting safeties Jordan Battle and Bryan Cook.

injuries.name: Colbie Young
injuries.headline: Young (knee) was not listed on the Bengals' injury report Wednesday.
injuries.notes: Young missed each of the Bengals' two games prior to the Week 6 bye due to a knee injury. The extra rest has paid dividends for the rookie fourth-rounder, who is on track to be available for Sunday's AFC North showdown against the Ravens. He's operated in a minimal role offensively this season, having logged only two catches on as many targets for nine yards across three games.

injuries.name: Josh Kattus
injuries.headline: The Bengals have signed Kattus to their practice squad.
injuries.notes: Kattus had been waived by the Bengals on Aug. 30, but the 6-foot-4, 247-pounder is now back with the team after not catching on elsewhere. In the process, the Kentucky product will provide added tight end depth behind Mike Gesicki, Drew Sample, Erick All and Jack Endries.

injuries.name: Tanner Hudson
injuries.headline: Hudson (pectoral) was placed on injured reserve by the Bengals on Monday.
injuries.notes: Hudson suffered a torn pectoral muscle during the team's 31-24 win over Miami in Week 5, so his transition to IR comes as no surprise. In his absence, Mike Gesicki, Drew Sample and Erick All will continue to operate as the team's primary options at tight end.

injuries.name: Dohnte Meyers
injuries.headline: Meyers brought in both of his targets for 12 yards during the Bengals' 31-24 win over the Dolphins on Sunday.
injuries.notes: Meyers entered Sunday on the heels of a huge performance on both offense and special teams during the Bengals' Week 4 loss to the Jaguars, when top pass catchers Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins sustained injuries. Chase and Higgins were both cleared to play against Miami and didn't face any restrictions in their respective snap counts, so Meyers reverted to a rotational role and was on the field for only 19 of Cincinnati's 65 offensive snaps (29.2 percent). The Bengals will enjoy their Week 6 bye before hitting the road for Week 7 against the Ravens on Sunday, Oct. 25.

injuries.name: Swayze Bozeman
injuries.headline: The Bengals placed Bozeman on injured reserve Monday due to a fractured forearm, Ben Baby of ESPN.com reports.
injuries.notes: The third-year linebacker out of Southern Miss sustained the injury during Sunday's 31-24 win over the Dolphins, and he'll now be sidelined for at least four weeks after landing on IR. Bozeman had suited up in four of the Bengals' first five contests of the season, seeing most of his action on special teams while tallying four tackles.

injuries.name: Evan McPherson
injuries.headline: McPherson made his lone field-goal attempt and all four of his extra-point tries during the Bengals' 31-24 win over the Dolphins on Sunday.
injuries.notes: McPherson was mostly limited to point-after tries thanks to four touchdown passes by Joe Burrow, but the former connected on a 26-yard chip shot late in the fourth quarter to extend Cincinnati's lead to 31-18. McPherson has attempted only one field goal in each of his last two games, but his scoring floor remains elevated on a week-to-week basis so long as the Bengals' offense under Burrow continues to move the ball down field. Cincinnati is on a bye for Week 6 before welcoming in Baltimore for Week 7 on Sunday, Oct. 25.

injuries.name: Samaje Perine
injuries.headline: Perine rushed 14 times for 68 yards while catching both of his targets for 10 yards and a touchdown during Sunday's 31-24 win over Miami.
injuries.notes: Perine surprisingly logged one more carry than starting running back Chase Brown (13) in the contest. Additionally, although he saw two fewer targets than Brown, Perine was able to reach paydirt in the second quarter, reeling in a six-yard touchdown pass from Joe Burrow. Perine remains a highly valuable insurance policy for fantasy managers with Brown on their roster. Through five games, the 31-year-old has rushed 27 times for 110 yards while reeling in seven of 10 targets for 61 yards and a score.

injuries.name: Mike Gesicki
injuries.headline: Gesicki brought in one of two targets for a four-yard touchdown in the Bengals' 31-24 win over the Dolphins on Sunday.
injuries.notes: Gesicki looked like he might be on his way to a big day against one of his former squads when he capped off the Bengals' lightning-fast opening possession with his scoring grab. However, the veteran tight end was a non-factor the rest of the way, posting his second-lowest totals over the first five games across all three categories of his receiving line. Gesicki's week-to-week production can certainly be difficult to trust, but he remains a trusted target of a prolific quarterback in what is still a pass-centric offense.

injuries.name: Tee Higgins
injuries.headline: Higgins brought in two of four targets for 22 yards in the Bengals' 31-24 win over the Dolphins on Sunday.
injuries.notes: Higgins was able to work through groin and neck injuries to suit up Sunday, but the veteran field-stretching receiver wasn't called on to do much on an afternoon when Joe Burrow threw for a season-low 192 yards. Nevertheless, Higgins seemingly made it through the game unscathed -- albeit with season-low totals across the board -- and he'll now have a Week 6 bye to further recover before a Week 7 road matchup against the Ravens on Sunday, Oct. 25.

injuries.name: Chase Brown
injuries.headline: Brown rushed 13 times for 39 yards and brought in three of four targets for 21 yards in the Bengals' 31-24 win over the Dolphins on Sunday. He also lost a fumble.
injuries.notes: As his final numbers corroborate, Brown found efficiency on the ground elusive against a surprisingly game Dolphins defense. The versatile back made a serviceable impact as a complementary option in the passing game, although his lost fumble came after a three-yard reception just past the midway point of the second quarter. Brown also saw Samaje Perine get some significant second-half run and ultimately outpace him by one rush attempt, but the former should remain the lead option in the ground attack coming out of a Week 6 bye in a Week 7 road matchup against the Ravens on Sunday, Oct. 25.

injuries.name: Joe Burrow
injuries.headline: Burrow completed 23 of 32 passes for 190 yards with four touchdowns and no interceptions and rushed four times for 10 yards in the Bengals' 31-24 win over the Dolphins on Sunday.
injuries.notes: Burrow averaged only 5.9 yards per attempt and finished with a season-low passing yardage total, but he offset the modest numbers by throwing a season-high number of touchdown passes. The prolific signal-caller benefited from having both Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins available after each carried questionable designations into Sunday, and he connected with Mike Gesicki (four yards), Samaje Perine (six yards), Tanner Hudson (two yards) and Ja'Marr Chase (45 yards) for his quartet of scoring tosses. Burrow spread the ball around to nine different targets overall, and he'll take an 11:3 TD:INT into a Week 7 road matchup against the Ravens on Sunday, Oct. 25, following a Week 6 bye.

injuries.name: Ja'Marr Chase
injuries.headline: Chase brought in six of 10 targets for 77 yards and a touchdown in the Bengals' 31-24 win over the Dolphins on Sunday.
injuries.notes: Chase was ultimately able to clear concussion protocol just before Sunday's game after exiting the Week 4 loss to the Jaguars with the head injury, and he finished as the Bengals' leader in all of receptions, receiving yards and targets against Miami. The star receiver capped off his productive day with a stellar one-handed, contested 45-yard touchdown grab in the waning moments of the third quarter. Chase is up to a 27-289-4 receiving line on the season despite having missed more than a half against Jacksonville, and he'll next tangle with the division-rival Ravens' veteran secondary in a Week 7 road matchup on Sunday, Oct. 25 following a Week 6 bye.

injuries.name: Bryan Cook
injuries.headline: Cook (ankle) is active for Sunday's game against Miami.
injuries.notes: Cook didn't play in Week 4 against Jacksonville but will return Sunday versus Miami, likely resulting in fewer defensive snaps for PJ Jules.

injuries.name: Demetrius Knight Jr.
injuries.headline: Knight finished Sunday's 22-17 loss to the Jaguars with six tackles (three solo).
injuries.notes: Linebacker Barrett Carter led the Bengals with 11 total tackles Sunday, with Knight finishing as the team's runner-up in that category. Knight's 45 defensive snaps (73.8 percent) were his fewest of the season after the second-year pro played at least 89.5 percent of the Bengals' defensive snaps in each of his first three games. He's up to 34 tackles (14 solo) and a scoop-and-score on the year.

injuries.name: Mitchell Tinsley
injuries.headline: Tinsley caught three of his seven targets for 49 yards in the Bengals' 22-17 loss to the Jaguars on Sunday.
injuries.notes: Tinsley's seven targets were fourth most among Bengals pass catchers behind Tee Higgins' (groin) 16, Chase Brown's 11 and Dohnte Meyers' nine. Tinsley stepped up after Ja'Marr Chase exited the contest with a concussion. Tinsley signed with the active roster Sept. 29 and likely will remain on it while the team deals with extensive injuries to the wide receiver corps.

injuries.name: Teven Jenkins
injuries.headline: The Browns placed Jenkins (back) on injured reserve Saturday.
injuries.notes: Jenkins has yet to play in the 2026 regular season due to a persistent back injury. The issue seems to be significant enough that Jenkins will not be able to return to the field soon, leaving the Browns no choice but to place the guard on IR.

injuries.name: Grant Delpit
injuries.headline: Delpit (concussion) does not have any injury designation ahead of Sunday's game against the Titans.
injuries.notes: Delpit was listed as questionable Friday but has cleared concussion protocol before Sunday's contest, as expected. The strong safety is set to suit up next to Ronnie Hickman to anchor the Browns' secondary as the team attempts to maintain its control of the AFC North.

injuries.name: Dylan Sampson
injuries.headline: Sampson (knee) was activated from injured reserve Saturday.
injuries.notes: Sampson also had his questionable injury designation removed and has been cleared to play against the Titans on Sunday. He's missed the Browns' last five games due to a knee injury, but his return means Cleveland's backfield will have its top backfield options in Sampson and Quinshon Judkins (ankle) for Week 7.

injuries.name: Jaleel McLaughlin
injuries.headline: McLaughlin's role in the offense could sharply decrease against the Titans on Sunday, as Quinshon Judkins (ankle) has been cleared to play and Dylan Sampson (knee) is expected to be activated off injured reserve, Daniel Oyefusi of ESPN.com reports.
injuries.notes: McLaughlin turned 13 touches (nine carries, four catches) into 55 yards in a Week 6 win against the Browns, but Cleveland was without Judkins, Sampson and Raheim Sanders (hip) for that contest. With Judkins and Sampson both on track to play Sunday, McLaughlin and Audric Estime will revert to depth roles on offense and will likely be limited to work on special teams.

injuries.name: Dillon Gabriel
injuries.headline: Gabriel (back) has been ruled out ahead of Sunday's game against the Titans, Zac Jackson of The Athletic reports.
injuries.notes: The Browns opened Gabriel's 21-day return window on Oct. 6. If the second-year quarterback is not activated by Tuesday's deadline, he will be forced to spend the remainder of the 2026 season on IR. The Browns have been struggling to make decisions at quarterback, so it remains unclear if the team will activate him, keep him stashed on IR, or waive him once a judgment call is forced.

injuries.name: Mason Graham
injuries.headline: Graham (knee/ankle) does not have any injury designation ahead of Sunday's game against the Titans, Zac Jackson of The Athletic reports.
injuries.notes: Graham missed consecutive games due to knee and ankle injuries but is ready to return to the field in Week 7. The second-year defensive tackle is all set to suit up alongside Maliek Collins in the contest, leaving Adin Huntington as the sole reserve option on the 53-man roster.

injuries.name: Mike Hall Jr.
injuries.headline: Hall (ankle) has been ruled out ahead of Sunday's game against the Titans, Zac Jackson of The Athletic reports.
injuries.notes: Hall will miss his third consecutive game with an ankle injury he suffered against the Steelers in Week 4. The defensive tackle's absence matters less now that Mason Graham has returned to the lineup to start alongside Maliek Collins. Hall's persistent injury means that Adin Huntington remains the only rotational defensive lineman on the 53-man roster.

injuries.name: Quincy Williams
injuries.headline: Williams (neck) is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Titans but expressed optimism Friday that he will play, Zac Jackson of The Athletic reports.
injuries.notes: Williams didn't practice Thursday due to a neck injury, but he was cleared to return for Friday's session, for which he was listed as a limited participant. The veteran linebacker told reporters that he was at full speed during Friday's practice, but his official status may not be known until 90 minutes before Sunday's 1:00 p.m. ET kickoff, which is when the Browns will announce their list of inactive players. If Williams cannot play, then Justin Jefferson and Winston Reid would be the top candidates to start alongside Carson Schwesinger and Easton Mascarenas-Arnold at linebacker.

injuries.name: Kalia Davis
injuries.headline: Davis (quadriceps) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Titans, Zac Jackson of The Athletic reports.
injuries.notes: Davis will remain on injured reserve through the Browns' Sunday contest against the Titans. The defensive tackle's 21-day practice window opened Oct. 6, meaning that if he is not activated by Tuesday, he will need to remain on IR for the rest of the 2026 season.

injuries.name: Denzel Ward
injuries.headline: Ward (hand) is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Titans, Zac Jackson of The Athletic reports.
injuries.notes: Ward appeared on the Browns' Friday injury report with a new hand injury. The cornerback managed to log a limited session despite the issue, but it remains uncertain whether he will be able to play through the injury in Sunday's contest. If Ward cannot suit up, Mekhi Blackmon or Toriano Pride will start at outside cornerback across from Tyson Campbell.

injuries.name: Quinshon Judkins
injuries.headline: Judkins (ankle) doesn't have an injury designation and said he's "good to go" for Sunday's game against the Titans, Mary Kay Cabot of the Cleveland Plain Dealer reports.
injuries.notes: Judkins also said he's excited to work with fellow running back Dylan Sampson, who is listed as questionable with an ankle injury. Sampson was expected to spell Judkins in a lot of passing situations this season, but the backup was injured on special teams in Week 1 and hasn't played since. Sampson's return could be bad news for Judkins' workloads, at least around the edges. He still projects as the clear lead back in Cleveland despite failing to kick-start the rushing attack so far.

injuries.name: Denzel Boston
injuries.headline: Boston (foot) doesn't have an injury designation for Sunday's game against the Titans, Zac Jackson of The Athletic reports.
injuries.notes: Boston played through the same injury last week and took 92 percent of Cleveland's snaps on offense in a 13-10 win over the Ravens. He caught just one of five targets for 15 yards, showing the downside of being a deep threat in an offense with poor QB play.

injuries.name: KC Concepcion
injuries.headline: Concepcion (calf/quadriceps) doesn't have an injury designation for Sunday's game against the Titans, Zac Jackson of The Athletic reports.
injuries.notes: Neither does fellow Browns wideout Denzel Boston, who has been limited in practice with a foot injury. There's been no indication that either WR was ever in serious danger of missing Sunday's game, so normal workloads can be expected unless there's an in-game setback.

injuries.name: Carson Schwesinger
injuries.headline: Schwesinger (ankle) was a limited participant at the Browns' practice Thursday.
injuries.notes: Schwesinger was able to return to the field after missing the team's first practice of the week while tending to his lingering ankle injury. The linebacker has been able to play through the injury the last few weeks, and he seems likely to be good to go Sunday versus the Titans.

injuries.name: Justin Jefferson
injuries.headline: Jefferson (hip) was a full participant at practice Wednesday, Mary Kay Cabot of The Cleveland Plain Dealer reports.
injuries.notes: Jefferson left the Browns' contest versus the Ravens in Week 6 early with a hip injury, but it looks like he'll be good to go for Week 7. Through two games in 2026, all 34 of his snaps have come on special teams.

injuries.name: Andre Szmyt
injuries.headline: Szmyt went 2-for-3 on field-goal attempts and made his only PAT during Sunday's 13-10 win over the Ravens.
injuries.notes: Szmyt made multiple field goals for the fifth week in a row. The kicker made his first try from 48 yards in the third quarter before missing another 48-yard try wide left with 3:44 left in regulation. Szmyt was able to get the last laugh though, nailing a game-winning 37-yard field goal as time expired in the fourth quarter. On the year, Szmyt has gone 12-for-13 on field-goal tries while making eight of nine extra-point attempts over six games.

injuries.name: Audric Estime
injuries.headline: Estime turned nine carries into 19 yards and a touchdown during the Browns' 13-10 win over the Ravens on Sunday.
injuries.notes: The Browns were without Quinshon Judkins (foot), Raheim Sanders (hip, IR) and Dylan Sampson (knee, IR) on Sunday, so Estime and Jaleel McLaughlin were the leaders of Cleveland's backfield. Estime and McLaughlin each had nine carries, but it was the former that logged a two-yard rushing touchdown midway through the fourth quarter to tie the game up at 10-10. Estime's 19 offensive snaps were nearly half of McLaughlin (39), but both of their roles will shrink significantly if Judkins is cleared to return for Week 7 against the Titans on Oct. 25.

injuries.name: Harold Fannin Jr.
injuries.headline: Fannin brought in one of three targets for nine yards in the Browns' 13-10 win over the Ravens on Sunday.
injuries.notes: Fannin was quiet for a second straight game while Jerry Jeudy surprisingly paced the Browns' air attack with a season-high 69 receiving yards. Fannin's production has been hard to trust during the first few weeks of the season, as he's recorded five or more catches just twice and three receptions and 27 receiving yards or less in his other four games. Fannin will look for a boost in his numbers during a Week 7 road matchup against the Titans on Sunday.

injuries.name: Dee Winters
injuries.headline: out
injuries.notes: out

injuries.name: Drew Shelton
injuries.headline: out
injuries.notes: out

injuries.name: KaVontae Turpin
injuries.headline: out
injuries.notes: out
injuries.vacated_opportunity_note: Expands to high-volume target progression and 2-WR/3-WR set route participation.

injuries.name: Cobie Durant
injuries.headline: Durant (hamstring) was a full participant in Friday's practice, Todd Archer of ESPN.com reports.
injuries.notes: Durant upgraded to a full participant in Friday's practice after being limited to start Week 7 prep Thursday. The cornerback has one more session to maintain his current participation standards in anticipation of Monday night's game against the Eagles.

injuries.name: P.J. Locke
injuries.headline: The Cowboys opened Locke's (foot) 21-day practice window Friday, Tommy Yarrish of the team's official site reports.
injuries.notes: The Cowboys placed Locke on injured reserve Sept. 26. The safety likely won't be available for Monday night's showdown with the Eagles, but Week 8 against the Cardinals is on the table. Locke will need to be activated by Nov. 13, or he must spend the remainder of the 2026 season on IR.

injuries.name: George Pickens
injuries.headline: Pickens (shoulder) was a full participant in Friday's practice, Tommy Yarrish of the Cowboys' official site reports.
injuries.notes: With Pickens upgrading from limited participation Thursday to full Friday, he appears to be good to go for Monday night against the Eagles. Pickens hasn't shown much of a fantasy ceiling to this point, outside of Week 5 against the Bucs when CeeDee Lamb was battling a quad issue, but few have the raw upside he possesses most weeks.

injuries.name: Marist Liufau
injuries.headline: The Cowboys designated Liufau (forearm) to return from injured reserve Thursday.
injuries.notes: The move opens Liufau's 21-day practice window, meaning the Cowboys can take up to three weeks to decide whether to activate the third-year defender or rule him out for the season. Liufau was a limited participant in practice Thursday, per Tommy Yarrish of the Cowboys' official site, and it's unclear if he'll be activated ahead of Monday's matchup in Philadelphia. Liufau was primarily a special-teamer last season and could take on a similar role as a rotational linebacker upon his potential return.

injuries.name: DeMarvion Overshown
injuries.headline: Overshown (hamstring) practiced in full Thursday, Jon Machota of The Athletic reports.
injuries.notes: Overshown hasn't played since suffering a hamstring injury Week 1 versus the Giants. However, director of player personnel Stephen Jones said Monday that the linebacker has a "great chance" to play in Week 7, and Overshown's return to action seems all but certain given his ability to log a full practice Thursday. Should he in fact suit up, Overshown should slide back in as a starter after logging a 74 percent defensive snap share in his lone appearance so far this season.

injuries.name: Caleb Downs
injuries.headline: Downs recorded 12 total tackles (six solo) during Sunday night's 23-13 loss to the Packers.
injuries.notes: Downs led the team in takedowns while notching a new career-high 12 stops in Week 6. The rookie hasn't missed a defensive snap since Week 1, and he has now produced 43 total tackles (25 solo), including 1.0 sacks, while also adding a pass defensed and two forced fumbles over the first six regular-season games of his career.

injuries.name: Juanyeh Thomas
injuries.headline: Thomas was signed to the Cowboys' active roster Tuesday.
injuries.notes: Thomas will officially join the active roster with Dallas after being elevated from the practice squad for each of the team's last three contests. The 26-year-old will provide the team with an additional experienced option at safety moving forward.

injuries.name: Brandon Aubrey
injuries.headline: Aubrey did not attempt any field goals but converted his only extra-point try during Sunday's 23-13 loss at Green Bay.
injuries.notes: In a game where the Cowboys fell into a hole early and turned the ball over three times in opposing territory, Aubrey was mostly a spectator, failing to make at least one field goal in a game for the first time since Week 1 against the Giants. Dallas' offense will have better days than it did Sunday, and one of those could come in Week 7 against a Philadelphia defense that has looked poor at times this season.

injuries.name: Javonte Williams
injuries.headline: Williams rushed 11 times for 41 yards and a touchdown while catching both of his targets for nine yards in Sunday's 23-13 loss to the Packers.
injuries.notes: Williams got the Cowboys on the board with a one-yard touchdown run in the third quarter. That was his seventh rushing score and eighth total touchdown through six games this season. Dallas trailed by double digits the entire second half, which explains Williams' season-low carry total. His frequent trips to the end zone have made up for a lack of efficiency, as Williams is averaging just 3.7 yards per carry after notching a career-best 4.8 YPC in 2025. Williams mustered 3.6 YPC in 2023 and 3.7 YPC in 2024 with the Broncos, so his first year in Dallas is starting to look like an outlier in that regard, though he should remain an effective fantasy option as long as he's locked into a three-down role with the Cowboys. He's likely to get more rushing opportunities in Week 7, as the Cowboys are unlikely to fall into a deep hole against an injury-riddled Eagles team on a four-game losing streak.

injuries.name: Dak Prescott
injuries.headline: Prescott completed 34 of 54 passes for 258 yards, one touchdown and two interceptions in Sunday's 23-13 loss to the Packers. He also rushed twice for seven yards.
injuries.notes: Prescott threw for just 86 yards with two interceptions in the first half, and the Cowboys took a 17-0 deficit into the locker room. He was only moderately more effective in the second half as Dallas looked out of sorts offensively for a second consecutive game in primetime. Prescott's lone touchdown pass was a six-yarder to Ryan Flournoy in the final minute of the fourth quarter. Dallas dropped to 2-4 with Sunday night's loss, and Dak has an ugly 4:4 TD:INT over his last four starts after posting a 6:1 mark through Week 2. Prescott will try to snap a two-game losing streak in Week 7 on MNF against the Eagles, who have dropped four straight.

injuries.name: Ryan Flournoy
injuries.headline: Flournoy caught seven of nine targets for 40 yards and a touchdown in Sunday night's 23-13 loss to the Packers.
injuries.notes: Flournoy has emerged as the clear third option in the passing game for Dallas, knocking an underperforming Jake Ferguson down the target totem pole. Flournoy's nine targets trailed CeeDee Lamb's 18 and George Pickens' 11 on a night where Dak Prescott attempted 54 passes. Flournoy found the end zone late with a six-yard score, and he's now posted 23 catches for 234 yards and one score on 36 targets through six games. He's an elite bench stash in the event something happens to Lamb or Pickens.

injuries.name: Jake Ferguson
injuries.headline: Ferguson caught two of three targets for 13 yards during Sunday night's 23-13 loss to the Packers.
injuries.notes: Ferguson matched his season low with two catches, and he has now been held to 23 or fewer yards in five of six contests to open the season. The tight end hasn't found the end zone since Week 3, and through six games, he's caught 17 of 24 targets for 115 yards and three scores. Ferguson reeled in a career-high 82 passes over 17 regular-season contests in 2025, and he has some work to do to return to that form in 2026.

injuries.name: CeeDee Lamb
injuries.headline: Lamb caught nine of 18 targets for 70 yards in Sunday's 23-13 loss to the Packers.
injuries.notes: Lamb led the Cowboys in catches and targets as he bounced back from a nine-yard performance in last Thursday's loss to the Buccaneers, during which he was bothered by a quadriceps contusion. After the Cowboys fell behind 17-0 at halftime, the star receiver gave the offense a spark on the team's first drive of the second half with a 17-yard catch to convert on fourth down. Javonte Williams eventually capped that possession with a touchdown run to get the Cowboys on the board, but Dallas didn't score again until the game's final minute. Lamb has drawn 69 targets heading into a Week 7 road game against the Eagles compared to 52 targets for George Pickens, who turned his 11 looks into a team-high 73 receiving yards in the loss to Green Bay.

injuries.name: Joey Porter Jr.
injuries.headline: Porter (ankle) is active for Sunday night's contest against Green Bay, Patrik Walker of the Cowboys' official site reports.
injuries.notes: Porter will return to action after missing the team's loss to Tampa Bay in Week 5 while nursing an ankle injury. The cornerback will be tasked with attempting to slow down the Packers' impressive vertical passing attack during Sunday Night Football.

injuries.name: Emari Demercado
injuries.headline: Demercado (coach's decision) is inactive for Sunday night's matchup with the Packers, Patrik Walker of the Cowboys' official site reports.
injuries.notes: Demercado was signed to the team's 53-man roster Tuesday, but he will ultimately take a seat in Week 6. In his absence, Javonte Williams and Tyler Goodson will handle the lion's share of the touches in the backfield.

injuries.name: Jonah Coleman
injuries.headline: The Broncos activated Coleman (ankle) from injured reserve Saturday, Jeremy Fowler of ESPN.com reports.
injuries.notes: Coleman is still questionable for Sunday's game against the Cardinals, but his activation off IR indicates that he is on track to appear in his first contest since Week 2 against the Jaguars. With Tyler Badie (thumb) on injured reserve, Coleman will slot into the RB3 spot behind J.K. Dobbins and RJ Harvey, and Coleman should also be in the mix for return duties on kickoffs.

injuries.headline: ir
injuries.notes: ir
