injuries.notes: questionable

injuries.name: Velus Jones Jr.
injuries.headline: Jones turned four carries into 20 yards and caught his only target for minus-1 yard during Thursday's 17-14 overtime loss to the Broncos.
injuries.notes: Jones played a total of 26 snaps (nine on offense, 17 on special teams) during Thursday's loss and operated as the clear RB3 behind Emanuel Wilson and George Holani. Jones was effective in the run game on limited carries, but he could lose his spot on the 53-man roster if Zach Charbonnet (knee) is activated from the reserve/PUP list ahead of the Seahawks' Week 7 home tilt against the Chiefs on Sunday, Oct. 25.

injuries.name: Tory Horton
injuries.headline: Horton caught one of five targets for 13 yards and returned a punt for 13 yards during the Seahawks' 17-14 overtime loss to the Broncos on Thursday. He also logged one tackle.
injuries.notes: Horton finished Thursday's game fourth on the Seahawks in targets but managed to catch only one pass from Sam Darnold, the latter of whom attempted a season-high 51 throws. Horton has a 5-67-1 receiving line on nine targets through five regular-season games, and he's firmly entrenched as the Seahawks' WR4 behind Jaxon Smith-Njigba, Cooper Kupp and Rashid Shaheed. The Seahawks will head back home for Week 7 to host the Chiefs on Sunday, Oct. 25.

injuries.name: Ernest Jones IV
injuries.headline: Jones recorded nine tackles (five solo), including 1.0 sacks, in Thursday night's 17-14 overtime loss to the Broncos.
injuries.notes: Jones has now recorded a sack in three straight games and has at least eight tackles in all six contests to kick off the 2026 campaign. He's up to 59 tackles (31 solo), including 3.0 sacks, and three pass breakups, with one interception, on 99.5 percent of the Seahawks' defensive snaps.

injuries.name: Jason Myers
injuries.headline: Myers went 2-for-3 on field-goal attempts during the Seahawks' 17-14 overtime loss to the Broncos on Thursday.
injuries.notes: Myers opened Thursday's scoring with a 55-yard field goal late in the first quarter, with the veteran kicker taking advantage of the altitude at Mile High Stadium. He missed a 47-yarder in the third quarter but made up for it with a 34-yard field goal within the final seconds of the fourth, which forced Thursday's game into overtime. It was the first missed field goal of the season for Myers, who is 12-for-13 on field-goal attempts (including 3-for-3 on kicks from 50-plus yards) and 14-for-15 on PATs through six regular-season games. The Seahawks will head back home for a Week 7 tilt against the Chiefs on Sunday, Oct. 25.

injuries.name: Cooper Kupp
injuries.headline: Kupp caught five of 10 targets for 50 yards during the Seahawks' 17-14 overtime loss to the Broncos on Thursday.
injuries.notes: Kupp accumulated 15 targets through the first five games of the regular season, but the veteran wide receiver was peppered Thursday by Sam Darnold, who attempted a season-high 51 passes. It was the first time since Week 12 of the 2024 season (with the Rams) that Kupp saw double-digit targets, and he finished second in that category Thursday behind Jaxon Smith-Njigba (16). Kupp's best days are behind him, but he's a valuable safety blanket for Darnold in the passing game. Kupp will bring a 16-179-1 receiving line (25 targets) into Seattle's Week 7 bout against the Chiefs on Sunday, Oct. 25.

injuries.name: AJ Barner
injuries.headline: Barner caught three of four passes for 16 yards during the Seahawks' 17-14 overtime loss to the Broncos on Thursday.
injuries.notes: Barner wasn't targeted by Sam Darnold until late in the third quarter, and he finished a distant fourth behind Jaxon Smith-Njigba, Rashid Shaheed and Cooper Kupp in both catches and receiving yards. Barner has played 90 percent or more of the Seahawks' offensive snaps in five of six games this season, but he's also caught more than three passes just once (Week 3 against the Commanders). He also doesn't have a touchdown to his name this season after finding the end zone six times during the 2025 regular season. The Seahawks will look to break their two-game losing streak in Week 7 on Sunday, Oct. 25 against the Chiefs, whose defense has given up the third-most fantasy points per game to tight ends this season.

injuries.name: Luke Goedeke
injuries.headline: Goedeke (calf) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Panthers.
injuries.notes: Goedeke missed the first two practices of Week 7 prep due to a calf issue, and while he returned in a limited capacity Friday, he will not be available for Sunday's NFC South tilt. The Buccaneers will have to turn to Justin Skule or Benjamin Chukwuma to start at right tackle in the absence of Goedeke, whose next chance to play is Week 8 against the Falcons on Sunday, Nov. 1.

injuries.name: Jalon Daniels
injuries.headline: Daniels is expected to work as Tampa Bay's No. 2 QB on Sunday in Carolina, as Baker Mayfield (thumb) is questionable to play but is expected to start, Scott Smith and Brianna Dix of the Buccaneers' official site report.
injuries.notes: Daniels has led Tampa Bay to a 1-2 record over his three starts in Mayfield's absence. The rookie has completed an acceptable 63.2 percent of his passes and has averaged 39 rush yards per game, but he's thrown four interceptions and just three touchdowns. While Mayfield still carries a questionable tag for Sunday, he was a full participant in practice all week, and coach Todd Bowles said the veteran signal-caller "looks like he's ready to go."

injuries.name: Zyon McCollum
injuries.headline: McCollum (illness) does not carry an injury designation into Sunday's game against the Panthers, Greg Auman of Fox Sports reports.
injuries.notes: McCollum opened the week as a DNP due to an illness, but he upgraded his practice participation over the next two days and has been cleared to play in Sunday's NFC South tilt. The fifth-year defensive back has 27 tackles (22 solo), seven pass defenses and one fumble recovery through six regular-season games.

injuries.name: Antoine Winfield Jr.
injuries.headline: Winfield (ribs) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against Carolina, Greg Auman of Fox Sports reports.
injuries.notes: Winfield was back on the practice field for Week 7 prep and was a limited participant in all three sessions. However, he has not been given the green light to return Sunday, so his next chance to suit up is Week 8 against the Falcons on Sunday, Nov. 1. Ifeatu Melifonwu figures to once again start alongside Tykee Smith at safety in Winfield's absence.

injuries.name: Tez Johnson
injuries.headline: Emeka Egbuka (concussion/foot) has been ruled out ahead of Sunday's game against the Panthers, so Johnson and the rest of the Buccaneers pass catchers will be tasked with larger roles offensively.
injuries.notes: Egbuka has seen at least nine targets in three of the Buccaneers' last four games, and those looks will be spread to Johnson, veteran Chris Godwin and rookie third-rounder Ted Hurst. The loss of Egbuka is significant for Tampa Bay's passing game, but the good news is franchise quarterback Baker Mayfield (thumb) appears on track to return from a three-game absence to play in Week 7. It's been an inconsistent season for Johnson, who has 20 receiving yards or less in four of six regular-season games and has a 7-145-0 receiving line on 13 targets.

injuries.name: Ted Hurst III
injuries.headline: Hurst and the other Buccaneers' wide receivers will have elevated roles against the Panthers on Sunday due to the absence of Emeka Egbuka (concussion/foot).
injuries.notes: Per Greg Auman of Fox Sports, Egbuka has gotten 43 percent of the targets and 31 percent of the receiving yards among Buccaneers' wide receivers. With Egbuka in concussion protocol, that workload will be taken on by Hurst, Tez Johnson and veteran Chris Godwin on Sunday against a Panthers defense that ranks fifth in the league in passing touchdowns allowed (six) and 18th in passing yards allowed per game (222.0). Hurst -- a third-round selection of the Buccaneers in the 2026 NFL Draft -- has an 11-168-1 receiving line on 22 targets through six regular-season games.

injuries.name: Bucky Irving
injuries.headline: Irving (illness) doesn't have an injury designation for Sunday's game at Carolina, Greg Auman of Fox Sports reports.
injuries.notes: Irving returned to practice Thursday as a limited participant before upgrading to full participation Friday. With WR Emeka Egbuka (concussion) ruled out and QB Baker Mayfield (thumb) on track to return from a three-game absence, Irving should see the ball early and often this Sunday.

injuries.name: Emeka Egbuka
injuries.headline: Egbuka (concussion) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Panthers, Greg Auman of Fox Sports reports.
injuries.notes: Buccaneers coach Todd Bowles previously indicated that Egbuka was doubtful to play, but the official designation is more definitive. Chris Godwin, Ted Hurst and Tez Johnson figure to take most of the WR snaps for the Buccaneers this Sunday at Carolina.
injuries.vacated_opportunity_note: Expands to high-volume target progression and 2-WR/3-WR set route participation.

injuries.name: Baker Mayfield
injuries.headline: Head coach Todd Bowles said Friday that Mayfield (right thumb) is ready for Sunday's game at Carolina, Greg Auman of Fox Sports reports.
injuries.notes: After missing Tampa Bay's last three games with a dislocated right thumb, Mayfield is expected to return to action against a Carolina team that's 2.5 games ahead of Tampa Bay in the NFC South standings. With wideout Emeka Egbuka (concussion/toe) listed as doubtful, Mayfield will likely look to Chris Godwin, Ted Hurst and Tez Johnson as his top targets at wide receiver.
injuries.vacated_opportunity_note: Takes over first-team reps under center with full pass-funnel responsibility.

injuries.name: Christian Rozeboom
injuries.headline: Rozeboom (finger) was placed on injured reserve by the Buccaneers on Thursday, Scott Smith of the team's official website reports.
injuries.notes: Rozeboom will be forced to miss at least four games while recovering from a finger injury that he likely suffered in Week 6 against the Steelers. In his absence, SirVocea Dennis will stand to see an increase in workload at inside linebacker behind starters Alex Anzalone and Josiah Trotter.

injuries.name: David Sills V
injuries.headline: Sills (hamstring) was activated from injured reserve by the Buccaneers on Thursday, Scott Smith of the team's official website reports.
injuries.notes: Sills had his 21-day practice window opened by the team Oct. 12, and he was able to open this week with back-to-back full practices. The wide receiver has been on IR since late August while recovering from a hamstring injury, but he will now slot in as a depth option behind Emeka Egbuka (concussion) and Chris Godwin moving forward this season.

injuries.name: Sean Tucker
injuries.headline: Tucker (quadriceps) was a full participant at practice Wednesday.
injuries.notes: Tucker was sidelined by a quad injury in Week 6 versus the Steelers, but it now appears he's on track to suit up again in Week 7. Regular starter Bucky Irving did not participate at practice Wednesday due to an illness, and if he was unavailable for any reason for Sunday's matchup at Carolina, Tucker would probably be looking at an expanded role in the Bucs' backfield.

injuries.name: Benjamin Morrison
injuries.headline: Morrison (quadriceps) was a full participant in Wednesday's practice.
injuries.notes: A quadriceps injury has sidelined Morrison for each of the Buccaneers' last three games, but his full session Wednesday indicates that he'll be available for Sunday's NFC South showdown against the Panthers. Morrison should reclaim his starting job at outside cornerback opposite Zyon McCollum (illness) while rookie fourth-rounder Keionte Scott reverts to a rotational role in the secondary.

injuries.name: Tykee Smith
injuries.headline: Smith compiled 10 total tackles (three solo) during Sunday's 26-19 overtime loss to the Steelers.
injuries.notes: Smith was able to record double-digit stops for the first time this season, finishing third on the team behind linebacker Josiah Trotter (12) and cornerback Zyon McCollum (11). Smith has now registered 34 total tackles (20 solo), a pass defensed and a forced fumble over the first six contests of the 2026 campaign.

injuries.name: Keionte Scott
injuries.headline: Scott recorded eight total tackles (four solo), including 1.0 sacks, during Sunday's 26-19 overtime loss to Pittsburgh.
injuries.notes: Scott was able to register a season-high eight tackles, most notably bringing down Aaron Rodgers for his first career sack in the second quarter. The cornerback has now compiled 32 total tackles (27 solo), including 1.0 sacks, while also adding two passes defensed over the first six regular-season games of his NFL career.

injuries.name: Josiah Trotter
injuries.headline: Trotter recorded 12 total tackles (five solo) and a pass defensed during Sunday's 26-19 overtime loss to the Steelers.
injuries.notes: Trotter was sharp again in Week 6, registering double-digit stops for the third time this season while playing every defensive snap in the loss. The linebacker has now registered 52 total tackles (27 solo), including 1.0 sacks, while also adding a pick-six over five games to open the 2026 campaign.

injuries.name: David Walker
injuries.headline: Walker recorded seven total tackles (four solo), including 2.0 sacks, during Sunday's 26-19 overtime loss to Pittsburgh.
injuries.notes: Walker was able to register a season-high seven stops, most notably getting to Aaron Rodgers for a pair of sacks in the third and fourth quarters. The linebacker has now compiled 17 total tackles (10 solo), including 4.0 sacks, over six games to open the 2026 campaign.

injuries.name: Chase McLaughlin
injuries.headline: McLaughlin connected on all four of his field-goal attempts and converted his lone extra-point try during the Buccaneers' 26-19 overtime loss to the Steelers on Sunday.
injuries.notes: It was the second time this season that McLaughlin made four field goals, including a 53-yarder in the dying seconds of the fourth quarter to force Sunday's game into overtime. He has yet to miss a kick this season, and his 14 made field goals are tied for third most in the NFL behind Spencer Shrader (18) and Will Reichard (15). The Buccaneers will be on the road for three of their next four games, starting with Week 7 against the Panthers on Oct. 25.

injuries.name: Cade Otton
injuries.headline: Otton caught one of two targets for four yards in Sunday's 26-19 overtime loss to the Steelers.
injuries.notes: Otton was targeted on just two of Jalon Daniels' 43 pass attempts, good for a lousy 4.7 percent share. The tight end has yet to catch a touchdown this season and has been held below 40 yards in five of six contests. He's a low-floor fantasy option at the position who is best left on waivers.

injuries.name: Chris Godwin Jr.
injuries.headline: Godwin caught four of eight targets for 37 yards in Sunday's 26-19 overtime loss to the Steelers.
injuries.notes: For the fifth time in six games to begin the season, Godwin caught either three or four passes, and all six of his yardage totals have been between 25 and 46 yards. The veteran wideout also has yet to score a TD in 2026, and his lackluster production has come whether Baker Mayfield (thumb) or rookie Jalon Daniels has been under center. Godwin will try to find a way to break out in Week 7 against the Panthers.

injuries.name: Kenny Gainwell
injuries.headline: Gainwell rushed two times for 17 yards in Sunday's 26-19 overtime loss to the Steelers. He caught his only target for seven yards.
injuries.notes: Even with Sean Tucker (quadriceps) inactive, Gainwell didn't see any sort of increase in his offensive role, getting out-carried 19 to two by Bucky Irving, who also saw three targets. Gainwell has 122 total yards through six games and can be sent to waivers in 10- and 12-team redraft fantasy leagues.

injuries.name: Timmy Horne
injuries.headline: The Titans signed Horne from the practice squad to the active roster Saturday, Jim Wyatt of the team's official site reports.
injuries.notes: Horne was elevated to the active roster for the Titans' Week 6 win over the Colts. The defensive tackle played 25 defensive snaps and three special-teams snaps in the contest, logging two tackles (one solo). Horne will now provide rotational value to the Titans' defensive line behind Jeffery Simmons and Solomon Thomas.

injuries.name: K.J. Osborn
injuries.headline: The Titans elevated Osborn from the practice squad to the active roster Saturday, Jim Wyatt of the team's official site reports.
injuries.notes: Osborn signed with the Titans' practice squad in early September but has not yet suited up for an NFL game in 2026. The wide receiver was likely elevated as insurance, set to be active only if Calvin Ridley (hip) cannot play in Sunday's contest due to injury.

injuries.name: Kalel Mullings
injuries.headline: The Titans elevated Mullings from the practice squad to the active roster Saturday, Jim Wyatt of the team's official site reports.
injuries.notes: Mullings receives his second elevation after suiting up for the Titans' Week 5 loss to the Texans. The running back played one offensive snap and 15 special-teams snaps in the contest, rushing just once for three yards.

injuries.name: Tony Adams
injuries.headline: Adams (ankle) is questionable for Sunday's game against the Browns, Jim Wyatt of the Titans' official site reports.
injuries.notes: Adams sustained an ankle injury during the Titans' Week 6 win over the Colts. He put together an LP-LP-FP practice log to draw the questionable tag, but if he cannot play, then Terrell Burgess may have to start alongside Amani Hooker at safety in the event that Kevin Winston (quadriceps) is also ruled out.

injuries.name: Kevin Winston Jr.
injuries.headline: Winston (quadriceps) is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Browns, Jim Wyatt of the Titans' official site reports.
injuries.notes: Winston has missed the Titans' last two games due to a quad injury, but he ended Week 7 prep with a full practice, giving him momentum toward a return for Sunday's home tilt. If Winston is cleared to play, then Tony Adams (ankle) would revert to a rotational role in the secondary.

injuries.name: Tyjae Spears
injuries.headline: Spears (knee) is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Browns, Jim Wyatt of the Titans' official site reports.
injuries.notes: Spears has been a mainstay on the Titans' injury report over the past few weeks due to ankle and knee issues. He put together a DNP-FP-LP practice log during Week 7 prep, but he has yet to miss a regular-season game. That said, Spears has seen minimal usage on offense this season, and his role figures to be limited unless lead back Tony Pollard were to miss time.
injuries.vacated_opportunity_note: Primary beneficiary of vacated early-down carries & red-zone volume if starter is sidelined.

injuries.name: Calvin Ridley
injuries.headline: Ridley (hip) will not practice Friday and is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against Cleveland, Turron Davenport of ESPN.com reports.
injuries.notes: Ridley and Elic Ayomanor have been splitting WR snaps alongside No. 1 receiver Carnell Tate and slot man Wan'Dale Robinson. If Ridley were to miss Sunday's game, Ayomanor presumably would take on more playing time.
injuries.vacated_opportunity_note: Expands to high-volume target progression and 2-WR/3-WR set route participation.

injuries.name: Dorian Mausi
injuries.headline: The Titans opened Mausi's 21-day practice window Wednesday, Jim Wyatt of the team's official website reports.
injuries.notes: Tennessee placed Mausi on injured reserve at the conclusion of the preseason due to a previously unspecified injury, but the team's first Week 7 injury report revealed that he's been working his way back from a foot issue. Mausi was able to turn in a full practice Wednesday, potentially giving him a shot at playing as soon as this Sunday versus the Browns if the Titans are willing to bring him back from IR.

injuries.name: Jeffery Simmons
injuries.headline: Simmons logged six tackles (three solo), including 2.0 sacks, one forced fumble and one fumble recovery during the Titans' 26-20 win over the Colts on Sunday.
injuries.notes: Simmons had just 1.0 sacks through five regular-season games, but he doubled that total during Sunday's win, which was Tennessee's first of the 2026 campaign. He stripped Jonathan Taylor of the football on the Colts' opening play of the third quarter and recovered the football himself, which led to a 29-yard field goal by Joey Slye seven plays later to put the Titans on the board. Simmons leads all defensive tackles with 34 combined stops through six regular-season games.

injuries.name: Amani Hooker
injuries.headline: Hooker logged 13 tackles (seven solo) and one interception during the Titans' 26-20 win over the Colts on Sunday.
injuries.notes: The Titans captured their first win of the season Sunday thanks largely to their defense and special teams. Hooker did his part with a game-high 13 combined tackles, and he made a toe-tap sideline interception off Daniel Jones late in the first quarter that stopped the Colts' red zone drive in its tracks. Hooker is up to 41 tackles (27 solo) and three pass defenses (including two interceptions) across five regular-season games and is on track to crack the tackling century mark for the first time in his eight-year NFL career.

injuries.name: Gunnar Helm
injuries.headline: Helm was on the field for 33 of 46 offensive snaps (71.7 percent) but didn't show up on the box score otherwise during the Titans' 26-20 win over the Colts on Sunday.
injuries.notes: Helm has seen his role on offense steadily decline since his four-catch performance in Week 1 against the Jets. He's been held without a catch in each of the last two games and has seen only two targets from Cam Ward over the Titans' last three games. Tennessee's offense is one of the worst units in the league this season, and it's hard to put much stock into any of the position players outside of rookie wide receiver Carnell Tate and, to a lesser extent, veteran running back Tony Pollard. The Titans will head back home for Week 7 against the Browns on Oct. 25,

injuries.name: Joey Slye
injuries.headline: Slye went 4-for-4 on field-goal tries and made both of his PATs during Sunday's 26-20 win over the Colts.
injuries.notes: Slye was able to make multiple field goals in a contest for the second time this season and for the first time since Week 2. The kicker converted attempts from 29 and 56 yards in the third quarter before adding makes from 49 and 44 yards in the fourth. Slye now has gone 9-for-10 on field-goal attempts, including 1-for-2 from 50-plus yards, while making all seven of his extra-point tries over six contests to open the 2026 campaign.

injuries.name: Wan'Dale Robinson
injuries.headline: Robinson caught three of seven targets for 22 yards during Sunday's 26-20 win over the Colts.
injuries.notes: Robinson finished tied for the team lead in targets with fellow wideout Carnell Tate, but he finished with 22 or fewer receiving yards for the second time in three weeks and the third time overall this season. The wide receiver, along with the rest of Tennessee's offense, is incredibly inconsistent, but he has seen at least five targets in four straight games.

injuries.name: Carnell Tate
injuries.headline: Tate caught six of seven targets for 70 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 26-20 win over the Colts.
injuries.notes: The rookie wideout capped a solid performance with an eight-yard TD in the fourth quarter, accounting for the Titans' only points on offense for the afternoon in their first win of 2026 and marking the first touchdown of his career. Tate's numbers were more remarkable considering that Cam Ward threw for a meager 102 yards in the game. Tate has begun to find a groove, posting a 22-279-1 line on 33 targets over his last four games. He'll look to keep rolling in Week 7 against the Browns.

injuries.name: Tony Pollard
injuries.headline: Pollard carried the ball 19 times for 76 yards and failed to catch his only target in Sunday's 26-20 win over the Colts.
injuries.notes: Tyjae Spears had only two touches as Pollard dominated work in the Titans backfield, and the veteran RB led the team in scrimmage yards on the afternoon. Pollard's 76 rushing yards were a season high, but he's gotten into the end zone just once in six games. He'll offer a solid floor, but little ceiling, in a Week 7 matchup against the Browns.

injuries.name: Cam Ward
injuries.headline: Ward completed 11 of 22 passes for 102 yards and one touchdown with one interception in Sunday's 26-20 win over the Colts. He added seven yards on three carries.
injuries.notes: The second-year QB put together his least productive game of the season, but Ward did connect with Carnell Tate for an eight-yard score in the fourth quarter. The Titans' special teams units accounted for the rest of their points in the team's first win of the year on four Joey Slye field goals and a blocked punt return for a TD. Ward has failed to reach 200 passing yards in five of six games to begin the season with a 4:4 TD:INT, giving him little fantasy appeal heading into a Week 7 tilt against the Browns.

injuries.name: Joshua Williams
injuries.headline: The Titans activated Williams (pectoral) from reserve/PUP on Saturday.
injuries.notes: The cornerback has also been cleared to play Sunday against the Colts after having his questionable tag removed. Williams will provide depth behind Alontae Taylor and Cor'Dale Flott at the position.

injuries.name: David Martin-Robinson
injuries.headline: Martin-Robinson (hamstring) does not have any injury designation ahead of Sunday's game against the Colts.
injuries.notes: Martin-Robinson upgraded to a full participant in Friday's practice after being limited to start Week 6 prep. The tight end is all set to suit up behind Gunnar Helm and Daniel Bellinger as the No. 3 tight end for the Titans' offense while also serving on special teams.

injuries.name: Cor'Dale Flott
injuries.headline: Flott (chest) was a full participant in Wednesday's practice session.
injuries.notes: Flott exited the Titans' Week 5 loss to the Texans early with a chest injury. The cornerback returned to the contest briefly after sustaining the chest injury before exiting again for the remainder of the night. Despite the injury, the 25-year-old is fully back in action just a few short days after the incident.

injuries.name: Jaylin Lane
injuries.headline: Lane underwent surgery Oct. 9 to repair his fractured and dislocated ankle, and he is expected to be cleared for activities before OTAs, Tashan Reed of The Washington Post reports.
injuries.notes: Lane sustained his season-ending ankle injury during the Commanders' Week 4 win against the Colts, and the injury was severe enough for him to stay in London overnight to be monitored and undergo additional tests. His absence has opened the door to more playing time for both Luke McCaffrey and Dyami Brown, and they are both candidates for another bump in playing time after Terry McLaurin tore his patellar tendon during the Commanders' 23-17 loss to the 49ers on Monday.
injuries.vacated_opportunity_note: Expands to high-volume target progression and 2-WR/3-WR set route participation.

injuries.name: Sonny Styles
injuries.headline: Styles finished Monday's 23-17 loss to the 49ers with 13 tackles (seven solo) and one pass defense.
injuries.notes: The rookie first-rounder led the Commanders in tackles Monday, and it was his second consecutive game with 13 combined tackles. Styles is up to 46 combined tackles through six regular-season games, which leads the Commanders and ranks in the top 20 in the NFL.

injuries.name: Drew Stevens
injuries.headline: Stevens made his only field-goal try and converted both of his extra-point attempts during Monday's 23-17 loss at San Francisco.
injuries.notes: The Commanders' offense put forth a mostly-uninspiring effort in Week 6, but Stevens made the most of his limited opportunities, including a 51-yard field goal to put the team on the scoreboard after its first drive of the night. Two-time Pro Bowl wide receiver Terry McLaurin ruptured his patellar tendon Monday, and regular starting running back Jacory Croskey-Merritt went to IR with a groin injury before the game, neither of which bodes well for Washington's general offensive outlook for the coming weeks. Stevens and the Commanders will take on the Eagles in Week 8 after their bye in Week 7.

injuries.name: Austin Ekeler
injuries.headline: Ekeler logged a three-yard carry and caught both of his targets for four yards during the Commanders' 23-17 loss to the 49ers on Monday.
injuries.notes: Despite the absence of Jacory Croskey-Merritt (groin), Ekeler was hardly involved in the Commanders' offensive game plan. He was on the field for only seven of 67 offensive snaps, well behind Rachaad White (45) and even fewer than the returning Jeremy McNichols (12). Even with Croskey-Merritt on IR for at least the next three games, It's hard to envision a path to consistent playing time for Ekeler following the Commanders' Week 7 bye.

injuries.name: Dyami Brown
injuries.headline: Brown hauled in his only target for six yards during Monday's 23-17 loss versus San Francisco.
injuries.notes: Despite Terry McLaurin (knee) exiting early in the loss to the 49ers, Brown wasn't on the field more than usual. He wasn't any more productive, either, catching just one pass for the second straight contest. McLaurin will miss the remainder of the 2026 campaign after it was announced Tuesday that he had been diagnosed with a torn left patellar tendon. However, that doesn't mean Brown will be more involved moving forward, considering the Commanders still have Antonio Williams, Stefon Diggs and Treylon Burks in the mix.

injuries.name: Jeremy McNichols
injuries.headline: McNichols accrued five rushes for 13 yards during Monday's 23-17 loss to the 49ers.
injuries.notes: With Jacory Croskey-Merritt (groin) sidelined, the Commanders turned to Rachaad White to do most of the heavy lifting at the running back position. McNichols, who was activated from injured reserve ahead of the Week 6 meeting with the 49ers after missing the first five games of the 2026 campaign, logged 12 offensive snaps, five more than Austin Ekeler (seven). However, neither McNichols nor Ekeler got anything going, with both players combining for six carries. With Croskey-Merritt now on injured reserve, there is room for others to step up, though it's likely White will remain the workhorse, with Ekeler and McNichols getting the leftover scraps.

injuries.name: Terry McLaurin
injuries.headline: Commanders head coach Dan Quinn announced Monday that McLaurin has been diagnosed with a torn patellar tendon in his left knee following an MRI and will miss the rest of the season.
injuries.notes: McLaurin went down with the injury on the Commanders' second possession of Monday's 23-17 loss to the 49ers. With McLaurin out of the mix for the rest of 2026, Stefon Diggs profiles as the Commanders' top wideout, while players such as Chig Okonkwo, Antonio Williams, Treylon Burks, Dyami Brown and Rachaad White could see their roles in the passing game expand further. McLaurin, who is under contract with Washington through 2028, finishes the season with 230 receiving yards and a touchdown on 15 receptions over five games.
injuries.vacated_opportunity_note: Expands to high-volume target progression and 2-WR/3-WR set route participation.

injuries.name: Charles Omenihu
injuries.headline: questionable
injuries.notes: questionable

injuries.name: Marcus Mariota
injuries.headline: doubtful
injuries.notes: doubtful
injuries.vacated_opportunity_note: Takes over first-team reps under center with full pass-funnel responsibility.

injuries.name: Treylon Burks
injuries.headline: Burks finished with four receptions for 66 yards on six targets in Monday's 23-17 loss to the 49ers.
injuries.notes: The reception, yardage and target totals were all season-best totals for Burks, whose heightened involvement in the passing game may have been a byproduct of No. 1 wideout Terry McLaurin (knee) exiting the game late in the first quarter. Though Burks didn't see a major spike in playing time compared to prior weeks -- he was on the field for 37 of 67 offensive snaps (55.2 percent) -- he should be able to maintain a regular role in three-receiver sets alongside Stefon Diggs and Antonio Williams, with McLaurin expected to miss time and potentially even being sidelined for the rest of the season.

injuries.name: Antonio Williams
injuries.headline: Williams brought in three of four targets for 50 yards in the Commanders' 23-17 loss to the 49ers on Monday night.
injuries.notes: Williams finished with the third-most receptions on the Commanders for the night, and the rookie posted the second-highest receiving yardage total of his nascent career. Williams has maintained a steady complementary presence in Washington's air attack while recording at least three catches in all but one game, and the third-round pick out of Clemson should continue filling a similar role when the Commanders return from a Week 7 bye in a home divisional battle against the Eagles on Sunday night, Nov. 1. His role could increase if Terry McLaurin's knee injury ends up being serious.

injuries.name: Chig Okonkwo
injuries.headline: Okonkwo brought in all seven targets for 69 yards in the Commanders' 23-17 loss to the 49ers on Monday night.
injuries.notes: The athletic tight end set the pace for the Commanders in receptions and receiving yards while also sharing the team lead in targets. It was Okonkwo's most productive performance yet over his brief four-game Commanders tenure, and the Maryland product looks like he's hitting his stride after missing Weeks 2 and 3 due to a hamstring injury. Okonkwo will head into a Week 7 bye with a combined 11-129-0 line on 13 targets over the last two games before returning to action at home against the Eagles on Sunday night, Nov. 1.

injuries.name: Rachaad White
injuries.headline: White rushed seven times for 27 yards and brought in four of five targets for 30 yards and a touchdown in the Commanders' 23-17 loss to the 49ers on Monday night.
injuries.notes: With Jacory Croskey-Merritt (groin) unavailable after landing on injured reserve prior to Monday's game, White worked as the de facto lead back. The ground attack took a back seat when the Commanders fell behind by a 20-3 margin going into intermission, but White was able to make an impact as a receiver. White posted his second receiving touchdown as a member of the Commanders, recording a nine-yard scoring grab in the fourth quarter for the final points of the night. With Croskey-Merritt out for at least three additional games, White could continue to see fairly solid volume in a Week 8 home matchup against the Eagles on Nov. 1 following the Commanders' Week 7 bye.

injuries.name: Jayden Daniels
injuries.headline: Daniels completed 29 of 40 passes for 300 yards with two touchdowns and no interceptions while adding four rushes for 10 yards in the Commanders' 23-17 loss to the 49ers on Monday night.
injuries.notes: Daniels' final numbers won't displease fantasy managers by any stretch, but the athletic signal-caller didn't really get the Commanders offense going until the second half. He put Washington's first touchdown of the night on the board in the waning seconds of the third quarter when he connected with Stefon Diggs from one yard out, and he followed it up with a 10-play, 90-yard march early in the fourth quarter that he capped off with a nine-yard touchdown toss to Rachaad White. However, Daniels and the Commanders came up empty on a subsequent 13-play drive that ended on downs, and the 2024 first-round pick then took a sack on the game's final play after triggering a 10-second runoff with an intentional grounding penalty on the prior snap. Despite the disappointing outcome, Daniels has been solid in his first two games back from an elbow injury, and he'll next face off with the Eagles at home on Sunday night, Nov. 1, following a Week 7 bye.

injuries.name: Javon Kinlaw
injuries.headline: Kinlaw (knee) won't return to Washington's matchup versus the 49ers on Monday, John Keim of ESPN reports.
injuries.notes: Kinlaw is done for the night after picking up a knee injury in the first half. He had previously dealt with a shoulder issue last month. In Kinlaw's absence, Shy Tuttle and Deatrich Wise should be in line for increased playing time for the remainder of Monday's game.

injuries.name: Tyler Owens
injuries.headline: Owens (hamstring) is active for Monday night's game against the 49ers.
injuries.notes: Owens logged consecutive limited practice sessions to end Week 6 prep. The backup strong safety has not yet played a defensive snap for the Commanders this season. Owens has played 91 special-teams snaps through the first five games of the season, logging six tackles (four solo).

injuries.name: Percy Butler
injuries.headline: Butler (hamstring) is active for Monday night's game against the 49ers.
injuries.notes: Butler returns to the lineup for the Commanders after missing the team's Week 5 tie with the Giants due to a hamstring injury. Butler will operate in his usual role as the backup at free safety to Jeremy Reaves.

injuries.name: Javontae Jean-Baptiste
injuries.headline: The Commanders placed Jean-Baptiste (pectoral) on injured reserve Monday.
injuries.notes: Jean-Baptiste was already ruled out for Monday night's game against the 49ers due to a pectoral injury, which is severe enough for the third-year pro to go on IR. He's required to miss at least four games, so the earliest he is eligible to return is Week 11 against the Bengals on Monday, Nov. 23.

injuries.name: Jordan Magee
injuries.headline: The Commanders activated Magee (hamstring) from injured reserve, and he is active for Monday night's game against the 49ers.
injuries.notes: Magee has been cleared to return from a four-game absence due to a hamstring injury that he sustained in Week 1 against the Eagles. The third-year pro is expected to work mostly on special teams, but his return bolsters the Commanders' depth at inside linebacker behind starters Frankie Luvu and rookie first-rounder Sonny Styles.

injuries.name: Nick Cross
injuries.headline: Cross (illness) is active for Monday night's game against the 49ers.
injuries.notes: Cross was a full participant in all three practices during Week 6 prep, and the fifth-year defensive back has been cleared by medical staff to return from a three-game absence due to an internal injury. His return means Quan Martin will revert to a depth role in the secondary for Monday night's game.

injuries.name: Trey Amos
injuries.headline: Amos (ankle) was activated from injured reserve by Washington on Monday.
injuries.notes: Amos is active for Monday night's matchup with the 49ers, returning to action after missing the team's first five games of the season while on IR with an ankle injury. The 24-year-old will likely slot in as one of the team's starting cornerbacks against San Francisco.
